9.3.4.s: prajāpater upahavyo 'niruktaḥ saptadaśānāṃ prathamo bhrātṛvyavān svargakāmaḥ paśukāmo vā yajeta /
9.3.4.d: प्रजापतेर् उपहव्यो ऽनिरुक्तः सप्तदशानां प्रथमो भ्रातृव्यवान् स्वर्गकामः पशुकामो वा यजेत /
9.3.4.m: The Upahavya of Prajāpati is unexpressed, the first among the seventeen[-versed rites]. One having a rival, one desiring heaven, or one desiring cattle should sacrifice [with it].

9.3.4.s: aśvaḥ śyāvo dakṣiṇā / sa brahmaṇe deyaḥ /
9.3.4.d: अश्वः श्यावो दक्षिणा / स ब्रह्मणे देयः /
9.3.4.m: A dark-brown horse is the sacrificial gift. That is to be given to the brahman priest.
The Ṛtapeya belongs to Soma, having the Bṛhat as its pṛṣṭha[-sāman]. Or one desiring a firm standing should sacrifice [with it].
There are nine initiations and three Upasad rites without the Pravargya.

9.3.4.s: ghṛtavratau bhavato varṣiṣṭhenāṅgulaparvaṇā samam anyacatuḥsthāne hrasiṣṭhenetarāsu /
9.3.4.d: घृतव्रतौ भवतो वर्षिष्ठेनाङ्गुलपर्वणा समम् अन्यचतुःस्थाने ह्रसिष्ठेनेतरासु /
9.3.4.m: There are two ghee-fasts; equal to the longest finger-joint in another four places, and to the shortest in the others.
Having spoken truth, they glide forward.
The procedure is established up to the time of the sacrificial gift.

9.3.4.s: somacamasaṃ kṛtasya rājño 'm̐śūnāṃ pūrṇaṃ dakṣiṇābhiḥ sahātihṛtya sagotrāya brahmaṇe dadāti / tena sa yajeta /
9.3.4.d: सोमचमसं कृतस्य राज्ञो ऽम्̐शूनां पूर्णं दक्षिणाभिः सहातिहृत्य सगोत्राय ब्रह्मणे ददाति / तेन स यजेत /
9.3.4.m: Having brought forward a Soma-cup filled with filaments of the prepared King [Soma] together with the sacrificial gifts, he gives it to a brahman priest of the same lineage. With that, he should sacrifice.
The Dūṇāśa belongs to Agni. One desiring heaven should sacrifice [with it].

9.3.4.s: āgneyam aṣṭākapālaṃ pūrvāhṇe nirvapet sauryaṃ carum ahany agnaye vaiśvānarāya dvādaśakapālam aparāhṇe cāndramasaṃ caruṃ naktam /
9.3.4.d: आग्नेयम् अष्टाकपालं पूर्वाह्णे निर्वपेत् सौर्यं चरुम् अहन्य् अग्नये वैश्वानराय द्वादशकपालम् अपराह्णे चान्द्रमसं चरुं नक्तम् /
9.3.4.m: One should apportion an eight-potsherd [cake] to Agni in the forenoon, a boiled oblation to Sūrya in the daytime, a twelve-potsherd [cake] to Agni Vaiśvānara in the afternoon, and a boiled oblation to Candramas at night.
At night, he performs the enclosing sacrifice for a half-month previously.

9.3.4.s: dīkṣaṇīyāyāṃ dvādaśamānaṃ prāyaṇīyāyām ātithyāyāṃ dve caturvim̐śatimāne dvistāvat tristāvad upasatsv agnīṣomīye savanīye savane 'nusavanam /
9.3.4.d: दीक्षणीयायां द्वादशमानं प्रायणीयायाम् आतिथ्यायां द्वे चतुर्विम्̐शतिमाने द्विस्तावत् त्रिस्तावद् उपसत्स्व् अग्नीषोमीये सवनीये सवने ऽनुसवनम् /
9.3.4.m: At the preparatory rite of initiation [he gives a piece of gold weighing] twelve measures; at the introductory rite and at the hospitality rite, two [pieces] of twenty-four measures; twice as much, three times as much during the Upasads, at the offering of the victim to Agni-Soma, at the pressing-victim, and pressing by pressing.
At the third pressing, when the Nārāśaṃsa [cups] are set down, at the concluding rite, [he gives] a garland to the udgātṛ priest.
A vaiśya desiring cattle should sacrifice with the Vaiśyastoma.
His offspring, however, becomes as if closed-eyed.

9.3.4.s: dhenuśatam āśire duhanti / tā eva dakṣiṇāḥ /
9.3.4.d: धेनुशतम् आशिरे दुहन्ति / ता एव दक्षिणाः /
9.3.4.m: They milk a hundred milch cows for the Soma-mixture. Those indeed are the sacrificial gifts.
On the fast-day, he has curds prepared from thirty-four of them.

9.3.4.s: prātaḥsavana upādhāya kapālāni ṣaṭṣaṣṭiṃ dohayaty ardham̐ śrapayati /
9.3.4.d: प्रातःसवन उपाधाय कपालानि षट्षष्टिं दोहयत्य् अर्धम्̐ श्रपयति /
9.3.4.m: At the morning pressing, having set up the potsherds, he milks sixty-six; half he boils.

9.3.4.s: saṃpūtam̐ rājānaṃ grahām̐ś ca pratiduhā pariṣiñcati śṛtena mādhyaṃdine /
9.3.4.d: संपूतम्̐ राजानं ग्रहाम्̐श् च प्रतिदुहा परिषिञ्चति शृतेन माध्यंदिने /
9.3.4.m: He pours fresh milk around the purified King [Soma] and the cups, [and] with boiled milk at the midday pressing.
The Kaṇvarathaṃtara is the pṛṣṭha[-sāman].

9.3.4.s: indrasya tīvrasud ukthyo rathaṃtarapṛṣṭhaḥ / somātipavito rājā yudhyāmāno grāmakāmo bhūtikāmaḥ pratiṣṭhākāmo vā yajeta /
9.3.4.d: इन्द्रस्य तीव्रसुद् उक्थ्यो रथंतरपृष्ठः / सोमातिपवितो राजा युध्यामानो ग्रामकामो भूतिकामः प्रतिष्ठाकामो वा यजेत /
9.3.4.m: The Tīvrasut belongs to Indra; it is an Ukthya rite having the Rathaṃtara as its pṛṣṭha[-sāman]. A king whose Soma has flowed away, one who is fighting, one desiring a village, one desiring prosperity, or one desiring a firm standing should sacrifice [with it].
He raises an altar extending as far as the sacrificial posts.
He sets up a set of eleven posts extending eastward.

9.3.4.s: garbhiṇīśatam āśire duhanti yathā vaiśyastome / vaḍavā ca garbhiṇyaḥ /
9.3.4.d: गर्भिणीशतम् आशिरे दुहन्ति यथा वैश्यस्तोमे / वडवा च गर्भिण्यः /
9.3.4.m: They milk a hundred pregnant cows for the Soma-mixture, as in the Vaiśyastoma, and pregnant mares.

9.3.4.d: अभक्षयन्तः स्वचमसान् उपोद्यछन्तो ऽत्राभ्युन्नीय जुह्वतः प्रचरन्ति /
9.3.4.m: Not consuming, raising up their own cups, pouring into [them] at this point, offering, they proceed.

9.3.4.s: adhvaryuś camasādhvaryavaś cāchāvākāya pratigīrya sarvabhakṣān bhakṣayanty adhvaryuś camasādhvaryavaś caivam uttarayoḥ savanayoḥ /
9.3.4.d: अध्वर्युश् चमसाध्वर्यवश् चाछावाकाय प्रतिगीर्य सर्वभक्षान् भक्षयन्त्य् अध्वर्युश् चमसाध्वर्यवश् चैवम् उत्तरयोः सवनयोः /
9.3.4.m: The adhvaryu and the cup-adhvaryus, having responded to the achāvāka priest, consume all the portions—the adhvaryu and the cup-adhvaryus—and thus in the two subsequent pressings.
The Vājapeya and the Rājasūya have been explained.

9.3.5.s: rāḍ virāṭ somasya rāḍ rājyam āśam̐samāno yajeta /
9.3.5.d: राड् विराट् सोमस्य राड् राज्यम् आशम्̐समानो यजेत /
9.3.5.m: The Rāj and the Virāj: the Rāj belongs to Soma; one hoping for sovereignty should sacrifice [with it].
The Virāj belongs to Agni; one desiring food should sacrifice [with it].
The Upasad and the Punastoma: the Upasads belong to Gandharvas and Apsarases; one desiring procreation should sacrifice [with it].

9.3.5.s: indrasya punastoma ukthyo yo bahu pratigṛhya garagīr iva manyeta yo vā madhyata ādīrṇa iva syāt sa etena yajeta /
9.3.5.d: इन्द्रस्य पुनस्तोम उक्थ्यो यो बहु प्रतिगृह्य गरगीर् इव मन्येत यो वा मध्यत आदीर्ण इव स्यात् स एतेन यजेत /
9.3.5.m: The Punastoma of Indra is an Ukthya rite. He who, having accepted much [in gifts], considers himself as if swallowing poison, or who is torn asunder from within, should sacrifice with this.
The Catuṣṭoma of Gautama: one desiring cattle should sacrifice [with it].
At the third pressing, having drawn the Ukthya [cup], he draws the Āgrayaṇa [cup].
The procedure is established up to the Agniṣṭoma cups.

9.3.5.d: अग्निष्टोमचमसान् उन्नीय पूर्ववद् ग्रहणसादनैर् होतृचमसे ऽवनयति /
9.3.5.m: Having drawn the Agniṣṭoma cups, he pours [them] into the hotṛ's cup with drawing and placing [formulas] as before.
The Udbhid and Balabhid belong to Bṛhaspati. One desiring cattle should sacrifice [with them].
Having sacrificed with the former, he should let a month elapse before the latter.
The two Apaciti rites belong to Prajāpati. One desiring reverence should sacrifice [with them].
Both have two sāmans, having the Bṛhat as their pṛṣṭha[-sāman].
The two Stomas of Agni: one desiring heaven should sacrifice [with them].
He carries the fire in the pan for a year. A thousand [cows are] the sacrificial gift.
The Ṛṣabha and Gosava rites belong to Indra.

9.3.5.s: ṛṣabho yaḥ kāmayetarṣabha iva samānānām̐ syām iti sa etena yajeta /
9.3.5.d: ऋषभो यः कामयेतर्षभ इव समानानाम्̐ स्याम् इति स एतेन यजेत /
9.3.5.m: The Ṛṣabha: he who should desire, 'May I be like a bull among my equals,' should sacrifice with this.
[The Ṛṣabha sacrifice] has both Sāmans and the Rathaṃtara as its Pṛṣṭha stotra.
One desirous of the highest position (parameṣṭhin) or desirous of fortune and kingship should sacrifice with the Gosava.
It is an Ukthya, having both Sāmans and the Bṛhat as its Pṛṣṭha stotra; ten thousand [cows] are the sacrificial gift.

9.3.5.s:
gāvo bhago gāva indro me achān \ gāvaḥ somasya prathamasya bhakṣaḥ /
imā yā gāvaḥ sa janāsa indras\ ichāmi hṛdā manasā cid indram //
iti māhendrakāle vācayitvā pārameṣṭhyāya \\ iti yathākāmaṃ pratiduhā pariṣiñcati /
9.3.5.d:
गावो भगो गाव इन्द्रो मे अछान् \ गावः सोमस्य प्रथमस्य भक्षः /
इमा या गावः स जनास इन्द्रस्\ इछामि हृदा मनसा चिद् इन्द्रम् //
इति माहेन्द्रकाले वाचयित्वा पारमेष्ठ्याय \\ इति यथाकामं प्रतिदुहा परिषिञ्चति /
9.3.5.m:
"Cows are fortune, cows may Indra provide for me; cows are the first draught of Soma.

These cows, O men, are Indra; I desire Indra with my heart and mind."

Having made him recite this at the time of the Māhendra cup, he pours [fresh milk] all around him with freshly milked milk according to wish, [saying]: "For the highest position!"

9.3.5.s: prajāpativid indravit stomakulāyau marutāṃ marutstomaḥ / puṣṭikāmo yajeta /
9.3.5.d: प्रजापतिविद् इन्द्रवित् स्तोमकुलायौ मरुतां मरुत्स्तोमः / पुष्टिकामो यजेत /
9.3.5.m: The Prajāpativid and Indravid are the two Stomakulāyas; the Marutstoma belongs to the Maruts. One desirous of thriving should sacrifice [with it].

9.3.5.s: indrāgnyoḥ kulāyo yaḥ kāmayeta kulāyam iva prajñāyāḥ paśūnām̐ syām iti sa etena yajetaitena yājayet /
9.3.5.d: इन्द्राग्न्योः कुलायो यः कामयेत कुलायम् इव प्रज्ञायाः पशूनाम्̐ स्याम् इति स एतेन यजेतैतेन याजयेत् /
9.3.5.m: The Kulāya of Indra and Agni: one who desires, 'May I be like a nest for offspring and cattle,' should sacrifice with this, or should cause [another] to sacrifice with this.

9.3.5.s: indrasyendrastoma ukthyo bṛhatpṛṣṭho rājyam āśam̐samāno yajeta /
9.3.5.d: इन्द्रस्येन्द्रस्तोम उक्थ्यो बृहत्पृष्ठो राज्यम् आशम्̐समानो यजेत /
9.3.5.m: Indra's Indrastoma is an Ukthya, having the Bṛhat as its Pṛṣṭha stotra; one expecting a kingdom should sacrifice [with it].
One hundred and twelve bulls are the sacrificial gift.

9.3.5.s: agneḥ stomo rājapurohitau sāyujyakāmau yajeyātām / purodhākāmo vā brāhmaṇaḥ /
9.3.5.d: अग्नेः स्तोमो राजपुरोहितौ सायुज्यकामौ यजेयाताम् / पुरोधाकामो वा ब्राह्मणः /
9.3.5.m: The Stoma of Agni: a king and his chaplain desirous of close union should sacrifice [with it], or a brāhmaṇa desirous of the office of domestic priest.
The Vighana: with it one desirous of cattle [should sacrifice].
One performing malevolent sorcery should sacrifice with the Saṃdaṃśa belonging to Indra.
He digs up an altar as long as the [eleven] sacrificial posts.
He sets up a set of eleven sacrificial posts facing east in a slanting place.
Twelve thousand bulls and a thousand horses are the sacrificial gift.

9.3.5.s: śrīṣṭomā dvādaśāgnimadukthyā vā / sarve 'yutadakṣiṇās taiḥ śrīkāmo yajeta /
9.3.5.d: श्रीष्टोमा द्वादशाग्निमदुक्थ्या वा / सर्वे ऽयुतदक्षिणास् तैः श्रीकामो यजेत /
9.3.5.m: The Śrīstomas are twelve, or [else are] Ukthyas containing Agni; all have ten thousand [cows] as sacrificial gifts. With them one desirous of prosperity should sacrifice.

9.3.5.s: ṛṣiṣṭomāḥ ṣoḍaśāptoryāmāḥ / sarve 'yutaprayutadakṣiṇās taiḥ sarvakāmo yajeta /
9.3.5.d: ऋषिष्टोमाः षोडशाप्तोर्यामाः / सर्वे ऽयुतप्रयुतदक्षिणास् तैः सर्वकामो यजेत /
9.3.5.m: The Ṛṣistomas are sixteen Aptoryāmas; all have ten thousand or a hundred thousand [cows] as sacrificial gifts. With them one desirous of everything should sacrifice.

9.3.6.s: teṣāṃ prajāpateḥ prathamo jyotir atirātra ṛddhikāmo yajeta /
9.3.6.d: तेषां प्रजापतेः प्रथमो ज्योतिर् अतिरात्र ऋद्धिकामो यजेत /
9.3.6.m: Among them, the first is Prajāpati's Jyotir-atirātra; one desirous of success should sacrifice [with it].
The Sarvastoma of Indra: one desirous of prosperity should sacrifice [with it].
Prajāpati's Aptoryāma has all the Pṛṣṭha stotras; one desirous of everything should sacrifice [with it].
Prajāpati's Navasaptadaśa: one desirous of offspring should sacrifice [with it].
Beginning with this, there are four Ṣoḍaśins.

9.3.6.s: ādityānām̐ stomo viṣuvāñ jyeṣṭho jyaiṣṭhineyo jyaiṣṭhyakāmo yajeta /
9.3.6.d: आदित्यानाम्̐ स्तोमो विषुवाञ् ज्येष्ठो ज्यैष्ठिनेयो ज्यैष्ठ्यकामो यजेत /
9.3.6.m: The Stoma of the Ādityas, the Viṣuvant: the eldest son born of the eldest wife, who desires pre-eminence, should sacrifice [with it].
One desirous of heaven [should sacrifice] with the Āyuṣṭoma.
One having a rival [should sacrifice] with the Abhijit.
Agni's Trivṛt: one desirous of fiery energy should sacrifice [with it].
Indra's Pañcadaśa: one desirous of virile vigor should sacrifice [with it].
Prajāpati's Saptadaśa: one desirous of food should sacrifice [with it].
The Āditya's Ekaviṃśa has the Bṛhat as its Pṛṣṭha stotra; one desirous of a firm foundation should sacrifice [with it].
Everywhere the night has fifteen-versed [stotras], and the dawn-twilight (saṃdhi) has the threefold [stoma].

9.3.7.s: paśum adbhiś cāturmāsyair yajeta /
9.3.7.d: पशुम् अद्भिश् चातुर्मास्यैर् यजेत /
9.3.7.m: He should perform the Cāturmāsya sacrifices accompanied by animal sacrifices.

9.3.7.s: eteṣām̐ vrataṃ kālaṃ dakṣiṇām̐ yathā haviryajñiyānām idhmābarhiḥ paurṇamāsīn vartanaṃ ca /
9.3.7.d: एतेषाम्̐ व्रतं कालं दक्षिणाम्̐ यथा हविर्यज्ञियानाम् इध्माबर्हिः पौर्णमासीन् वर्तनं च /
9.3.7.m: The observance, time, and sacrificial gift of these are like those of the Haviryajñas; [likewise] the sacrificial fuel and grass, the full-moon days, and the course [of rites].

9.3.7.s: tasyatasya parvaṇaḥ purastāt pāśuky ārambhaṇīyā /
9.3.7.d: तस्यतस्य पर्वणः पुरस्तात् पाशुक्य् आरम्भणीया /
9.3.7.m: Before each respective seasonal knot (parvan), an introductory animal rite is performed.

9.3.7.s: vaiśvadevena yajeta /
9.3.7.d: वैश्वदेवेन यजेत /

9.3.7.s: cātvālaprabhṛti vyāghāraṇāntaṃ lupyate /
9.3.7.d: चात्वालप्रभृति व्याघारणान्तं लुप्यते /
9.3.7.m: [The acts] beginning with the sounding hole (cātvāla) and ending with the sprinkling with clarified butter are omitted.

9.3.7.s: śvobhūte vaiśvadevaḥ paśuḥ /
9.3.7.d: श्वोभूते वैश्वदेवः पशुः /
9.3.7.m: On the next day, there is an animal victim for the Viśve Devas.

9.3.7.s: siddham ā niyojanāt /
9.3.7.d: सिद्धम् आ नियोजनात् /

9.3.7.s: madhyame paridhau paśuṃ niyunakti paridhiśakalena svarukarmotakare vā cātvālakarma sarvam /
9.3.7.d: मध्यमे परिधौ पशुं नियुनक्ति परिधिशकलेन स्वरुकर्मोतकरे वा चात्वालकर्म सर्वम् /
9.3.7.m: He tethers the animal victim to the middle enclosing stick; the ritual act of the wooden chip (svaru) is performed with a chip of an enclosing stick, or the entire sounding-hole ritual is performed at the rubbish heap (utkara).

9.3.7.s: vājinena caritvā vāpanakāle nivartayati /
9.3.7.d: वाजिनेन चरित्वा वापनकाले निवर्तयति /
9.3.7.m: Having performed the offering of the whey (vājina), he causes [the sacrificer's hair] to turn back at the time of shaving.

9.3.7.s: caturo māsān na mām̐sam aśnātīti vyākhyātam /
9.3.7.d: चतुरो मासान् न माम्̐सम् अश्नातीति व्याख्यातम् /
9.3.7.m: "For four months he does not eat meat" has been explained.

9.3.7.s: varuṇapraghāseṣu pūrvāṃ paurṇamāsīm upoṣya mārutīṃ meṣīm ālabheta /
9.3.7.d: वरुणप्रघासेषु पूर्वां पौर्णमासीम् उपोष्य मारुतीं मेषीम् आलभेत /
9.3.7.m: At the Varuṇapraghāsa rites, having fasted on the prior full-moon day, he should seize a female sheep for the Maruts.

9.3.7.s: uttaravedim /
9.3.7.d: उत्तरवेदिम् /

9.3.7.s: minoti yūpam̐ yūpe niyunakti /
9.3.7.d: मिनोति यूपम्̐ यूपे नियुनक्ति /
9.3.7.m: He sets up a sacrificial post; he tethers [the victim] to the sacrificial post.

9.3.7.s: asam̐sṛṣṭe 'ntaḥparidhy aṅgārān dakṣiṇāpohya karambhapātrāṇi juhoti /
9.3.7.d: असम्̐सृष्टे ऽन्तःपरिध्य् अङ्गारान् दक्षिणापोह्य करम्भपात्राणि जुहोति /
9.3.7.m: When they are not in contact, having pushed the glowing embers southward inside the enclosing sticks, he offers the dishes of groats (karambhapātra).

9.3.7.s: hutāyām̐ vapāyāṃ cātvāle mārjayitvā vāruṇyai vatsān apākaroti /
9.3.7.d: हुतायाम्̐ वपायां चात्वाले मार्जयित्वा वारुण्यै वत्सान् अपाकरोति /
9.3.7.m: When the omentum has been offered, having purified [themselves] at the sounding hole, he drives away the calves for the offering to Varuṇa.

9.3.7.s: na svaruṃ juhoti / na yūpam anupadiśati /
9.3.7.d: न स्वरुं जुहोति / न यूपम् अनुपदिशति /
9.3.7.m: He does not offer the chip of the post; he does not assign the sacrificial post.

9.3.7.s: auttaravedike 'gnihotraṃ juhoti /
9.3.7.d: औत्तरवेदिके ऽग्निहोत्रं जुहोति /
9.3.7.m: He offers the Agnihotra on the fire of the high altar.

9.3.7.s: śvobhūte vāruṇo meṣa paśuḥ /
9.3.7.d: श्वोभूते वारुणो मेष पशुः /
9.3.7.m: On the next day, the animal victim is a ram for Varuṇa.

9.3.7.s: avabhṛthād udetya vāruṇapraghāsikena caritvā yūpam anudiśati /
9.3.7.d: अवभृथाद् उदेत्य वारुणप्रघासिकेन चरित्वा यूपम् अनुदिशति /
9.3.7.m: Having emerged from the purifying bath (avabhṛtha) and having performed the rite of the Varuṇapraghāsas, he assigns the sacrificial post.

9.3.7.s: vāpanakāle nivartayati /
9.3.7.d: वापनकाले निवर्तयति /
9.3.7.m: At the time of shaving, he causes [his hair] to turn back.

9.3.7.s: caturo māsān na mām̐sam aśnātīti vyākhyātam /
9.3.7.d: चतुरो मासान् न माम्̐सम् अश्नातीति व्याख्यातम् /
9.3.7.m: "For four months he does not eat meat" has been explained.

9.3.7.s: sākamedheṣu pūrvayāṃ paurṇamāsyām āgneyaḥ paśuru ttarasyām aindrāgno yajanīye vā prājāpatya ekādaśinā vā paśuḥ /
9.3.7.d: साकमेधेषु पूर्वयां पौर्णमास्याम् आग्नेयः पशुरु त्तरस्याम् ऐन्द्राग्नो यजनीये वा प्राजापत्य एकादशिना वा पशुः /
9.3.7.m: At the Sākamedhas, an animal victim for Agni is [offered] on the prior full-moon day; on the later [full-moon day], on the day of sacrifice, an animal victim for Indra and Agni, or one for Prajāpati, or an eleven-victim set.

9.3.7.s: avabhṛthād udetya pitṛyajñena caranty ata ekolmukena tryambakān yanti /
9.3.7.d: अवभृथाद् उदेत्य पितृयज्ञेन चरन्त्य् अत एकोल्मुकेन त्र्यम्बकान् यन्ति /
9.3.7.m: Having emerged from the purifying bath, they perform the ancestral sacrifice; taking a single firebrand from this, they go to the Tryambaka offerings.

9.3.7.s: pratyetyāparasminn agnitantra ādityena caritvā yūpam anudiśati /
9.3.7.d: प्रत्येत्यापरस्मिन्न् अग्नितन्त्र आदित्येन चरित्वा यूपम् अनुदिशति /
9.3.7.m: Having returned, having performed [the rite] with the [caru] dedicated to Āditya in the subsequent fire-framework, he points to the sacrificial post.

9.3.7.s: vāpanakāle nivartayati /
9.3.7.d: वापनकाले निवर्तयति /
9.3.7.m: At the time of shaving, he desists [from shaving].

9.3.7.s: caturo māsān na mām̐sam aśnātīti vyākhyātam /
9.3.7.d: चतुरो मासान् न माम्̐सम् अश्नातीति व्याख्यातम् /
9.3.7.m: It is explained by the rule: 'For four months he does not eat meat.'

9.3.7.s: śunāsīrye vāyavyaḥ paśur upām̐śudevataḥ / sa vaiśvadevena vyākhyātaḥ /
9.3.7.d: शुनासीर्ये वायव्यः पशुर् उपाम्̐शुदेवतः / स वैश्वदेवेन व्याख्यातः /
9.3.7.m: At the Śunāsīrya, the animal sacrifice is for Vāyu, its deity [invoked] in a whisper. It is explained by the Vaiśvadeva.

9.3.7.s: pratiparvahavīm̐ṣi paśupuroḍāśeṣv anvāyātayati / yathā devikās tair upām̐śu tathā pracaranti /
9.3.7.d: प्रतिपर्वहवीम्̐षि पशुपुरोडाशेष्व् अन्वायातयति / यथा देविकास् तैर् उपाम्̐शु तथा प्रचरन्ति /
9.3.7.m: He causes the oblations of each joint-festival to follow along with the animal cakes. As in the case of the Devikā oblations, so they proceed with them in a whisper.

9.3.7.s: varuṇapraghāseṣu sapta pūrvasmin vāruṇy ekakapālāv uttarasmin /
9.3.7.d: वरुणप्रघासेषु सप्त पूर्वस्मिन् वारुण्य् एककपालाव् उत्तरस्मिन् /
9.3.7.m: At the Varuṇapraghāsa rites, there are seven [oblations] in the first, and two single-potsherd [cakes] for Varuṇa in the subsequent one.

9.3.7.s: sākamedheṣv anīkavatsāṃtapanau prathame yathākālaṃ gṛhamedhīyapūrṇadarvyau madhyame krīḍinam uttame /
9.3.7.d: साकमेधेष्व् अनीकवत्सांतपनौ प्रथमे यथाकालं गृहमेधीयपूर्णदर्व्यौ मध्यमे क्रीडिनम् उत्तमे /
9.3.7.m: At the Sākamedha rites, the Anīkavat and the Sāṃtapana are in the first [part]; at their proper times, the Gṛhamedhīya and the Pūrṇadarvī are in the middle [part]; the Krīḍin is in the last [part].

9.3.7.s: mahāhavīm̐ṣi śunāsīrye cāmnātaḥ paśuḥ sāmo vā /
9.3.7.d: महाहवीम्̐षि शुनासीर्ये चाम्नातः पशुः सामो वा /
9.3.7.m: The Mahāhavis oblations and the animal sacrifice are taught in the Śunāsīrya, or [alternatively] as a Soma sacrifice.

9.3.8.m: One should sacrifice with the seasonal Four-Month sacrifices in Soma form.

9.3.8.s: vaiśvadevasya loke trivṛd agniṣṭomo daśa dīkṣās tisra upasadaḥ /
9.3.8.d: वैश्वदेवस्य लोके त्रिवृद् अग्निष्टोमो दश दीक्षास् तिस्र उपसदः /
9.3.8.m: In place of the Vaiśvadeva, there is a ninefold Agniṣṭoma, ten consecrations, and three Upasads.
He omits the sacrificial post and the high altar.
On the dhiṣṇya hearths he makes only marks.
After the Hāriyojana cup, they perform the rite with the whey.
Having come out from the purificatory bath, [wearing] an unwashed garment, the post-sacrificial animal is dedicated to Bṛhaspati.
At the time of shaving, he desists [from shaving].

9.3.8.s: caturo māsān na mām̐sam aśnātīti vyākhyātam /
9.3.8.d: चतुरो मासान् न माम्̐सम् अश्नातीति व्याख्यातम् /
9.3.8.m: It is explained by the rule: 'For four months he does not eat meat.'

9.3.8.s: varuṇapraghāsānām̐ loke dvyahaḥ / ṣoḍaśa dīkṣā dvādaśopasadaḥ /
9.3.8.d: वरुणप्रघासानाम्̐ लोके द्व्यहः / षोडश दीक्षा द्वादशोपसदः /
9.3.8.m: In place of the Varuṇapraghāsa rites, there is a two-day sacrifice, sixteen consecrations, and twelve Upasads.
The first [day] is the Jyotir-Agniṣṭoma.
He heaps up the high altar at the dhiṣṇya hearths.
He erects the sacrificial post; he binds [the victim] to the sacrificial post.

9.3.8.s: prātaḥsavane dhiṣṇyeṣu vihṛteṣu mārjālīye 'gnim upadhārayet karambhapātrebhyaḥ /
9.3.8.d: प्रातःसवने धिष्ण्येषु विहृतेषु मार्जालीये ऽग्निम् उपधारयेत् करम्भपात्रेभ्यः /
9.3.8.m: At the morning pressing, when the fires have been distributed to the dhiṣṇya hearths, he should place fire on the Mārjālīya for the vessels of groats.
On the fourteenth day, he sacrifices to Varuṇa with the husks and residue of Varuṇa.
Having returned, the post-sacrificial victim is for Mitra and Varuṇa.
At the time of shaving, he desists [from shaving].

9.3.8.s: caturo māsān na mām̐sam aśnātīti vyākhyātam /
9.3.8.d: चतुरो मासान् न माम्̐सम् अश्नातीति व्याख्यातम् /
9.3.8.m: It is explained by the rule: 'For four months he does not eat meat.'

9.3.8.s: sākamedhānām̐ loke tryahaḥ / pañcadaśa dīkṣā dvādaśopasadaḥ /
9.3.8.d: साकमेधानाम्̐ लोके त्र्यहः / पञ्चदश दीक्षा द्वादशोपसदः /
9.3.8.m: In place of the Sākamedha rites, there is a three-day sacrifice, fifteen consecrations, and twelve Upasads.
There are an Agniṣṭoma, an Ukthya, and an Atirātra.

9.3.8.s: caturdaśyāṃ tṛtīyasya tṛtīyasavane dhiṣṇyeṣu vihṛteṣu mārjālīye 'gnim upasamādhāya pitṛyajñāyodayanīyād ūrdhvam̐ pitṛyajñena caranti /
9.3.8.d: चतुर्दश्यां तृतीयस्य तृतीयसवने धिष्ण्येषु विहृतेषु मार्जालीये ऽग्निम् उपसमाधाय पितृयज्ञायोदयनीयाद् ऊर्ध्वम्̐ पितृयज्ञेन चरन्ति /
9.3.8.m: On the fourteenth day of the third [day's rite], at the third pressing, when the fires have been distributed to the dhiṣṇya hearths and fire has been placed on the Mārjālīya for the ancestral sacrifice, they proceed with the ancestral sacrifice after the concluding rite.
From here, with a single firebrand, they go to the Tryambaka offerings.
Having returned, the post-sacrificial victim is a barren cow for Sūrya.
He causes the boiled oblation for Āditya to follow after the animal cake.
At the time of shaving, he desists [from shaving].

9.3.8.s: caturo māsān na māṃsam aśnātīti vyākhyātam /
9.3.8.d: चतुरो मासान् न मांसम् अश्नातीति व्याख्यातम् /
9.3.8.m: It is explained by the rule: 'For four months he does not eat meat.'

9.3.8.s: śunāsīryasya loke trivṛd agniṣṭomo jyotir agniṣṭomaḥ /
9.3.8.d: शुनासीर्यस्य लोके त्रिवृद् अग्निष्टोमो ज्योतिर् अग्निष्टोमः /
9.3.8.m: In place of the Śunāsīrya, there is a ninefold Agniṣṭoma, a Jyotir-Agniṣṭoma.
The post-sacrificial victim is for the Aśvins; it is explained by the Vaiśvadeva.
He causes the oblations of each joint-festival to follow along with the morning-pressing offerings, as in the animal sacrifices.

9.3.8.s: purā vasatīvarīṇāṃ pariharaṇād gṛhamedhīyaḥ / purā prātaranuvākāt pūrṇadarvī yathā paśumatsu /
9.3.8.d: पुरा वसतीवरीणां परिहरणाद् गृहमेधीयः / पुरा प्रातरनुवाकात् पूर्णदर्वी यथा पशुमत्सु /
9.3.8.m: Before carrying around the Vasatīvarī waters, the Gṛhamedhīya [takes place]; before the morning recitation, the Pūrṇadarvī [takes place], as in the animal sacrifices.
Those which are the animals [appointed] are the daily pressing-victims.

9.3.8.s: pañcāśad dakṣiṇā uttame dvādaśam̐ śatam uttame dvādaśam̐ śatam /
9.3.8.d: पञ्चाशद् दक्षिणा उत्तमे द्वादशम्̐ शतम् उत्तमे द्वादशम्̐ शतम् /
9.3.8.m: The sacrificial gift is fifty; on the last day, one hundred and twelve; on the last day, one hundred and twelve.

9.4.1.s: upariṣṭādatirātrā dvyahaprabhṛtayo 'hīnā dvādaśāhaparyantāḥ /
9.4.1.d: उपरिष्टादतिरात्रा द्व्यहप्रभृतयो ऽहीना द्वादशाहपर्यन्ताः /
9.4.1.m: Beginning with the two-day sacrifice and ending with the twelve-day sacrifice are Ahīna rites having an Atirātra at the end.

9.4.1.s: paurṇamāsīdīkṣāḥ /
9.4.1.d: पौर्णमासीदीक्षाः /

9.4.1.s: māsāpavargā upasadaḥ satyānām̐ śeṣeṇa / dīkṣā anyatravacanāt /
9.4.1.d: मासापवर्गा उपसदः सत्यानाम्̐ शेषेण / दीक्षा अन्यत्रवचनात् /
9.4.1.m: The Upasads terminate with the month, according to the rest of the Satya [rules]; the consecrations [are as stated], unless specified otherwise.

9.4.1.s: tatraikāhikaśabdeṣv aikāhikā dharmā daśarātrikā itareṣu /
9.4.1.d: तत्रैकाहिकशब्देष्व् ऐकाहिका धर्मा दशरात्रिका इतरेषु /
9.4.1.m: There, regarding the designations of one-day rites, the rules of one-day rites [apply]; in the others, [the rules] of the ten-day period [apply].

9.4.1.s: yathā pṛṣṭhyā grahāgrāṇi tryanīkā vā /
9.4.1.d: यथा पृष्ठ्या ग्रहाग्राणि त्र्यनीका वा /
9.4.1.m: According to the Pṛṣṭhya [order], the first cups [are drawn], or in three troops.

9.4.1.s: ekādaśinān samadhā vibhajed uttamam uttame 'pi vā /
9.4.1.d: एकादशिनान् समधा विभजेद् उत्तमम् उत्तमे ऽपि वा /
9.4.1.m: He should divide the eleven victims equally, or [place] the last one on the last [day].

9.4.1.s: aikāhikaśabdeṣu kratupaśava ekādaśinā itareṣu /
9.4.1.d: ऐकाहिकशब्देषु क्रतुपशव एकादशिना इतरेषु /
9.4.1.m: In the designations of one-day rites, there are sacrifice-animals; in the others, the set of eleven [victims].

9.4.1.s: āṅgiraso dvyahānāṃ prathamas tena yajeta yaḥ puṇyo hīna iva manyeta prajākāmaḥ paśukāmo vā /
9.4.1.d: आङ्गिरसो द्व्यहानां प्रथमस् तेन यजेत यः पुण्यो हीन इव मन्येत प्रजाकामः पशुकामो वा /
9.4.1.m: The Āṅgirasa is the first of the two-day sacrifices; one who, though meritorious, considers himself degraded, or one desirous of offspring, or one desirous of cattle, should sacrifice with it.

9.4.1.s: jyotir agniṣṭomaḥ pūrvam̐ sarvastomo 'tirātraḥ ṣoḍaśimān uttaram /
9.4.1.d: ज्योतिर् अग्निष्टोमः पूर्वम्̐ सर्वस्तोमो ऽतिरात्रः षोडशिमान् उत्तरम् /
9.4.1.m: The first day is the Jyotir-Agniṣṭoma; the subsequent day is an all-stoma Atirātra with the Ṣoḍaśin.

9.4.1.s: caitrarathena rājā vijigīṣamāṇo yajeta /
9.4.1.d: चैत्ररथेन राजा विजिगीषमाणो यजेत /
9.4.1.m: A king wishing to conquer should sacrifice with the Caitraratha.

9.4.1.s: jyotir ukthyaḥ pūrvam āyur atirātraḥ ṣoḍaśimān uttaram /
9.4.1.d: ज्योतिर् उक्थ्यः पूर्वम् आयुर् अतिरात्रः षोडशिमान् उत्तरम् /
9.4.1.m: The first day is the Jyotir-Ukthya; the subsequent day is the Āyus-Atirātra with the Ṣoḍaśin.

9.4.1.s: kāpivanena yajeta ya iched arūkṣaḥ paśumān syām iti yo vā paśumān rūkṣa iva manyeta prajākāmaḥ paśukāmo vā /
9.4.1.d: कापिवनेन यजेत य इछेद् अरूक्षः पशुमान् स्याम् इति यो वा पशुमान् रूक्ष इव मन्येत प्रजाकामः पशुकामो वा /
9.4.1.m: One who desires 'May I become rich in cattle without suffering dryness,' or one who possesses cattle and considers himself as though dry, or one desirous of offspring, or one desirous of cattle, should sacrifice with the Kāpivana.

9.4.1.s: trivṛtpañcadaśo 'gniṣṭomaḥ pūrvam̐ sarvastomo 'tirātraḥ ṣoḍaśimān uttaram /
9.4.1.d: त्रिवृत्पञ्चदशो ऽग्निष्टोमः पूर्वम्̐ सर्वस्तोमो ऽतिरात्रः षोडशिमान् उत्तरम् /
9.4.1.m: The first day is an Agniṣṭoma of ninefold and fifteenfold [chants]; the subsequent day is an all-stoma Atirātra with the Ṣoḍaśin.

9.4.1.s: viśveṣāṃ devānāṃ gargatrirātraḥ / sarvakāmo yajetāmuṃ ca lokam abhijigīṣan /
9.4.1.d: विश्वेषां देवानां गर्गत्रिरात्रः / सर्वकामो यजेतामुं च लोकम् अभिजिगीषन् /
9.4.1.m: The Garga three-day sacrifice belongs to the Viśvedevas; one desiring all things, or one wishing to conquer that world, should sacrifice [with it].

9.4.1.s: daśarātrasyāditas tryahas tasyāntare ahanī viparīte / tasmin rātriḥ saṣoḍaśikā /
9.4.1.d: दशरात्रस्यादितस् त्र्यहस् तस्यान्तरे अहनी विपरीते / तस्मिन् रात्रिः सषोडशिका /
9.4.1.m: It consists of the three days from the beginning of the ten-day period, but its inner two days are reversed; on it, there is a night [rite] with the Ṣoḍaśin.

9.4.1.s: saptasaptānvaham āśire duhanti /
9.4.1.d: सप्तसप्तान्वहम् आशिरे दुहन्ति /
9.4.1.m: Daily they milk seven [cows] each for the milk-mixture.

9.4.1.s: dakṣiṇākāle trirūpā paṣṭuhī rūpasaṃpannā sahasratamy upakḷptā /
9.4.1.d: दक्षिणाकाले त्रिरूपा पष्टुही रूपसंपन्ना सहस्रतम्य् उपकॢप्ता /
9.4.1.m: At the time of the sacrificial gifts, a three-coloured six-year-old cow endowed with marks is prepared as the thousandth.

9.4.1.s: trayastrim̐śataṃ trīṇi ca śatāni dadāti /
9.4.1.d: त्रयस्त्रिम्̐शतं त्रीणि च शतानि ददाति /
9.4.1.m: He gives three hundred and thirty-three [cows].

9.4.1.s:
tāsu tv avasthitāsu
tvaksahasram airaya \ ud balasyābhi nas tvacam /
sa naḥ sahasram ā bhara \ vasumān vasubhiḥ saha //
punar māviśatā́m̐ rayiḥ //
ity unnatasya dakṣiṇe karṇe yajamāno japati //
9.4.1.d:
तासु त्व् अवस्थितासु
त्वक्सहस्रम् ऐरय \ उद् बलस्याभि नस् त्वचम् /
स नः सहस्रम् आ भर \ वसुमान् वसुभिः सह //
पुनर् माविशता́म्̐ रयिः //
इत्य् उन्नतस्य दक्षिणे कर्णे यजमानो जपति //
9.4.1.m:
“You have aroused a thousand-fold skin; / raise our skin to strength!

Bring to us a thousand, / rich in treasures, along with the Vasus!

The sacrificer mutters into the right ear of the tall [bull].

9.4.1.s: ubhā jigyathur ity āgnīdhrīye pūrṇāhutiṃ juhoti /
9.4.1.d: उभा जिग्यथुर् इत्य् आग्नीध्रीये पूर्णाहुतिं जुहोति /
9.4.1.m: With "You two have both conquered…", he offers the full oblation into the āgnīdhra fire.

9.4.1.s: utsṛṣṭā anumantrayate /
9.4.1.d: उत्सृष्टा अनुमन्त्रयते /
9.4.1.m: He accompanies [the cows] that have been let loose with a mantra:

9.4.1.s:
iha sādhanaḥ pūro na āgād \ yo gopāḥ puṣṭipatir va āgāt /
asmākaṃ kāmam upakāmino viśve devāḥ //
upasṛja paśūn iha \ iho śakeva puṣyata /
ihaivota pra jāyadhvam \ asmān vardhayatā naraḥ //
ni vartadhvaṃ mānu gāta\ asmān siṣakta revatīḥ /
agnīṣomā punarvasū \ asme dhārayatam̐ rayim //
punar enā ā vartaya \ mayi tiṣṭhantu gopatau /
punar enā ā vartaya \ mayi tiṣṭhatu yo rayiḥ //
jātavedo ni vartaya \ śataṃ te santv āvṛtaḥ \ sahasraṃ ta upāvṛtaḥ /
athā poṣasya poṣeṇa \ punar no naṣṭam ākṛdhi \ punar no rayim ākṛdhi //
punar ūrjā \ saha rayyā \\ ūrjā vaḥ paśyāmi \\ iti goyajñas tāsām /
9.4.1.d:
इह साधनः पूरो न आगाद् \ यो गोपाः पुष्टिपतिर् व आगात् /
अस्माकं कामम् उपकामिनो विश्वे देवाः //
उपसृज पशून् इह \ इहो शकेव पुष्यत /
इहैवोत प्र जायध्वम् \ अस्मान् वर्धयता नरः //
नि वर्तध्वं मानु गात\ अस्मान् सिषक्त रेवतीः /
अग्नीषोमा पुनर्वसू \ अस्मे धारयतम्̐ रयिम् //
पुनर् एना आ वर्तय \ मयि तिष्ठन्तु गोपतौ /
पुनर् एना आ वर्तय \ मयि तिष्ठतु यो रयिः //
जातवेदो नि वर्तय \ शतं ते सन्त्व् आवृतः \ सहस्रं त उपावृतः /
अथा पोषस्य पोषेण \ पुनर् नो नष्टम् आकृधि \ पुनर् नो रयिम् आकृधि //
पुनर् ऊर्जा \ सह रय्या \\ ऊर्जा वः पश्यामि \\ इति गोयज्ञस् तासाम् /
9.4.1.m:
“Here has arrived our completing leader, / he who is protector of cattle, master of nourishment, has come to you.

May all the gods be desirous of our desire!

Release the cattle here; / thrive here like dung!

Right here be prolific; / O men, make us flourish!

Turn back, do not wander away; / accompany us, O opulent ones!

O Agni and Soma, who bring back treasures, / uphold wealth in us!

Turn these back again; / let them stay with me, the lord of cows!

Turn these back again; / let whatever wealth there is stay with me!

O Jātavedas, turn them back; / let there be a hundred turns for you, a thousand returns for you!

Then with the prosperity of prosperity, / make what was lost return to us; make wealth return to us!”

With “Again with sap…”, “Together with wealth…”, “With sap I behold you…”, [is recited] their sacrifice to cows.

9.4.1.s: ya ārṣeyo vidvām̐s tasmai śataṃ dadāti /
9.4.1.d: य आर्षेयो विद्वाम्̐स् तस्मै शतं ददाति /
9.4.1.m: He gives a hundred to him who is of ṛṣi lineage and learned.

9.4.1.s: madhyame dvitīyaṃ tāsu vehat tasyāḥ karṇe \\ ūrg asi \\ ūrjaṃ mayi dhehi \ punar māviśatām̐ rayir iti /
9.4.1.d: मध्यमे द्वितीयं तासु वेहत् तस्याः कर्णे \\ ऊर्ग् असि \\ ऊर्जं मयि धेहि \ पुनर् माविशताम्̐ रयिर् इति /
9.4.1.m: On the middle [day], the second [third of the gift], among them a cow that miscarries, into her ear: “You are sap; place sap in me! May wealth enter into me again!”

9.4.1.s: yo 'nārṣeyo vidvām̐s tasmai śatam /
9.4.1.d: यो ऽनार्षेयो विद्वाम्̐स् तस्मै शतम् /
9.4.1.m: He gives a hundred to him who is not of ṛṣi lineage but learned.

9.4.1.s: sahasratamīṃ dakṣiṇāpathena nītvottarata uttaravedes tāṃ darbheṇa prachādya prāṅmukhām avasthāpayati /
9.4.1.d: सहस्रतमीं दक्षिणापथेन नीत्वोत्तरत उत्तरवेदेस् तां दर्भेण प्रछाद्य प्राङ्मुखाम् अवस्थापयति /
9.4.1.m: Having led the thousandth [cow] by the southern path, having covered her with darbha grass to the north of the high altar, he makes her stand facing east.

9.4.1.s:
ā jighra kalaśaṃ mahi /
ā tvā viśantv indavaḥ \ samudram iva sindhavaḥ //
sā naḥ sahasraṃ dhukṣva\ urudhārā payasvatī /
prajayā sūnṛte saha \ punar māviśatām̐ rayiḥ //
iti droṇakalaśam avaghrāpayati //
9.4.1.d:
आ जिघ्र कलशं महि /
आ त्वा विशन्त्व् इन्दवः \ समुद्रम् इव सिन्धवः //
सा नः सहस्रं धुक्ष्व\ उरुधारा पयस्वती /
प्रजया सूनृते सह \ पुनर् माविशताम्̐ रयिः //
इति द्रोणकलशम् अवघ्रापयति //
9.4.1.m:
May the soma drops enter you, / like rivers into the sea!

Milk for us a thousand, / wide-flowing, full of milk!

Along with offspring, O true one, / may wealth enter into me again!”

With these words he makes her sniff the wooden trough.

9.4.1.s: kāmyāsi \ priyāsi \ havyāsi \\ iḍe rante juṣṭe sarasvati mahi viśrute \\ etāni te 'ghnye nāmāni \ deveṣu naḥ sukṛto brūyād iti gonāmāni dakṣiṇe karṇe yajamāno japati /
9.4.1.d: काम्यासि \ प्रियासि \ हव्यासि \\ इडे रन्ते जुष्टे सरस्वति महि विश्रुते \\ एतानि ते ऽघ्न्ये नामानि \ देवेषु नः सुकृतो ब्रूयाद् इति गोनामानि दक्षिणे कर्णे यजमानो जपति /
9.4.1.m: “You are desirable; you are dear; you are fit for oblations; O Iḍā, Rantā, beloved, Sarasvatī, great, renowned! These are your names, O unslayable cow; speak of us among the gods as doers of good deeds!”—with these cow names the sacrificer mutters into her right ear.

9.4.1.s: tasyā daśakalā brahmaṇe dadāti pañcāgnīdhe //
9.4.1.d: तस्या दशकला ब्रह्मणे ददाति पञ्चाग्नीधे //
9.4.1.m: He gives ten parts of her to the brahman priest, five to the āgnīdhra priest.

9.4.1.s: ekā mama \\ ity āhitām̐ yajamānasya goṣṭhe visṛjati /
9.4.1.d: एका मम \\ इत्य् आहिताम्̐ यजमानस्य गोष्ठे विसृजति /
9.4.1.m: With “One is mine”, he releases the one placed in the cowpen of the sacrificer.

9.4.1.s: annam etābhyāṃ tārpyaṃ ca dadāti tasya dvibhāgaṃ brahmaṇe /
9.4.1.d: अन्नम् एताभ्यां तार्प्यं च ददाति तस्य द्विभागं ब्रह्मणे /
9.4.1.m: He gives food and a silk garment to these two; of it, two shares to the brahman priest.

9.4.1.s:
uttame tṛtīyaṃ tāsu vāmanaḥ
pratiṣṭhāsi sahasrasya \ vaiṣṇavo vāmanas tvam /
sa naḥ pratiṣṭhām ā bhara \ vasumān vasubhiḥ saha //
punar māviśatām̐ rayiḥ //
iti /
9.4.1.d:
उत्तमे तृतीयं तासु वामनः
प्रतिष्ठासि सहस्रस्य \ वैष्णवो वामनस् त्वम् /
स नः प्रतिष्ठाम् आ भर \ वसुमान् वसुभिः सह //
पुनर् माविशताम्̐ रयिः //
इति /
9.4.1.m:
On the final [day], the third [share], among them a dwarf [bull]:

“You are the firm foundation of the thousand, / you are the dwarf belonging to Viṣṇu.

Bring to us a firm foundation, / rich in treasures, along with the Vasus!

9.4.1.s: ya ārṣeyo 'vidvām̐s tasmai śatam /
9.4.1.d: य आर्षेयो ऽविद्वाम्̐स् तस्मै शतम् /
9.4.1.m: He gives a hundred to him who is of ṛṣi lineage but unlearned.

9.4.1.s: yathā gargatrirātra evam ekaikam̐ sāhasraṃ datvā sahasratamīkarma karoti /
9.4.1.d: यथा गर्गत्रिरात्र एवम् एकैकम्̐ साहस्रं दत्वा सहस्रतमीकर्म करोति /
9.4.1.m: As in the Garga three-day rite, thus having given each of the thousand-parts, he performs the rite of the thousandth [cow].

9.4.1.s: prajāpater aśvatrirātraḥ sa vyākhyātaḥ /
9.4.1.d: प्रजापतेर् अश्वत्रिरात्रः स व्याख्यातः /
9.4.1.m: The horse-three-day rite of Prajāpati: that has been explained.

9.4.1.s: indrāgnyor vaidatrirātro rājā vijigīṣamāṇo yajeta /
9.4.1.d: इन्द्राग्न्योर् वैदत्रिरात्रो राजा विजिगीषमाणो यजेत /
9.4.1.m: The Vaida three-day rite of Indra and Agni: a king desiring victory should perform this sacrifice.

9.4.1.s: trayastrivṛto 'tirātrāḥ ṣoḍaśimantaḥ /
9.4.1.d: त्रयस्त्रिवृतो ऽतिरात्राः षोडशिमन्तः /
9.4.1.m: There are three trivṛt atirātra days, having the ṣoḍaśin cups.

9.4.1.s: ādityānāṃ chāndomaḥ ... /
9.4.1.d: आदित्यानां छान्दोमः ... /

9.4.1.s: ... parākaḥ / svargakāmo yajeta /
9.4.1.d: ... पराकः / स्वर्गकामो यजेत /
9.4.1.m: […] Parāka; one desiring heaven should sacrifice.

9.4.1.s: gargatrirātreṇa vyākhyāta etad devānām eṣayet /
9.4.1.d: गर्गत्रिरात्रेण व्याख्यात एतद् देवानाम् एषयेत् /
9.4.1.m: It is explained by the Garga three-day rite. He should seek this for the gods.

9.4.2.s: atreś caturvīraś catūrātrāṇāṃ prathamo ya ichec catvāro me vīrā ājāyerann iti sa etena yajeta /
9.4.2.d: अत्रेश् चतुर्वीरश् चतूरात्राणां प्रथमो य इछेच् चत्वारो मे वीरा आजायेरन्न् इति स एतेन यजेत /
9.4.2.m: The Four-Hero [sacrifice] of Atri is the first of the four-day rites; he who desires, “May four hero-sons be born to me,” should sacrifice with this.
There are an agniṣṭoma, two ukthya days, and an atirātra.

9.4.2.d: जमदग्नेर् द्वितीयो ऽपरिमितां पुष्टिम् इछन् यजेत /
9.4.2.m: The second [four-day rite is that] of Jamadagni; one desiring unlimited prosperity should sacrifice.
There are twenty consecration days and twelve upasad days.
After each upasad he cooks sacrificial cakes that have been prepared silently.
Having decorated them, he deposits them along with clarified butters.

9.4.2.s: upasadā pracarya \\ agne ver hotram̐ ver adhvaram \ ā pitaram̐ vaiśvānaram avase kar \ indrāya devebhyo juhutām̐ havir ity ṛjuṃ pratiṣṭhitam̐ hutvopasadaṃ juhoti / tathāparāhṇikyām /
9.4.2.d: उपसदा प्रचर्य \\ अग्ने वेर् होत्रम्̐ वेर् अध्वरम् \ आ पितरम्̐ वैश्वानरम् अवसे कर् \ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुताम्̐ हविर् इत्य् ऋजुं प्रतिष्ठितम्̐ हुत्वोपसदं जुहोति / तथापराह्णिक्याम् /
9.4.2.m: Having performed the upasad rite, having offered [a cake] placed straight with: “O Agni, accept the hotṛ's office, accept the solemn rite; invoke father Vaiśvānara for help! Sacrifice the oblation for Indra, for the gods!”, he offers the upasad oblation; likewise in the afternoon [rite].

9.4.2.s: etena vai dharmeṇottarāsu dvikapālaṃ trikapālaṃ kapālābhyuccayenā dvādaśakapālāt //
9.4.2.d: एतेन वै धर्मेणोत्तरासु द्विकपालं त्रिकपालं कपालाभ्युच्चयेना द्वादशकपालात् //
9.4.2.m: In this very manner, on the subsequent [days], there are cakes on two potsherds, on three potsherds, with an increase of potsherds up to twelve potsherds.

9.4.2.s: devāv aśvinau madhukaśayādyemam̐ yajñam̐ yajamānāya mimikṣatam \ indrāya devebhyo juhutām̐ havir \ deva viṣṇa urv adyāsmin yajñe yajamānāya vikramasva \\ indrāya devebhyo juhutām̐ havir \ deva soma retodhā adyāsmin yajñe yajamānāyaidhi \\ indrāya devebhyo juhutām̐ havir \ deva dhātaḥ sudhātādyāsmin yajñe yajamānāyaidhi \\ indrāya devebhyo juhutā́m̐ havir \ devā grāvāṇo madhumatīm adyāsmin yajñe yajamānāya vācam̐ vadata \\ indrāya devebhyo juhutām̐ havir \ devy anumate 'nv adyemam̐ yajñam̐ yajamānāya manyasva \\ indrāya devebhyo juhutām̐ havir \ devy adite svādityam adyāsmin yajñe yajamānāyāsuvasva \\ indrāya devebhyo juhutām̐ haivḥ \ sadaḥsadaḥ prajāvān ṛbhur juṣāṇo jñas \\ indrāya devebhyo juhutām̐ havir \ deva tvaṣṭaḥ suretodhā adyāsmin yajñe yajamānāyaidhi \\ indrāya devebhyo juhutām̐ havir iti svāhākārāntair ādadhāti /
9.4.2.d: देवाव् अश्विनौ मधुकशयाद्येमम्̐ यज्ञम्̐ यजमानाय मिमिक्षतम् \ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुताम्̐ हविर् \ देव विष्ण उर्व् अद्यास्मिन् यज्ञे यजमानाय विक्रमस्व \\ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुताम्̐ हविर् \ देव सोम रेतोधा अद्यास्मिन् यज्ञे यजमानायैधि \\ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुताम्̐ हविर् \ देव धातः सुधाताद्यास्मिन् यज्ञे यजमानायैधि \\ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुता́म्̐ हविर् \ देवा ग्रावाणो मधुमतीम् अद्यास्मिन् यज्ञे यजमानाय वाचम्̐ वदत \\ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुताम्̐ हविर् \ देव्य् अनुमते ऽन्व् अद्येमम्̐ यज्ञम्̐ यजमानाय मन्यस्व \\ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुताम्̐ हविर् \ देव्य् अदिते स्वादित्यम् अद्यास्मिन् यज्ञे यजमानायासुवस्व \\ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुताम्̐ हैव्ः \ सदःसदः प्रजावान् ऋभुर् जुषाणो ज्ञस् \\ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुताम्̐ हविर् \ देव त्वष्टः सुरेतोधा अद्यास्मिन् यज्ञे यजमानायैधि \\ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुताम्̐ हविर् इति स्वाहाकारान्तैर् आदधाति /
9.4.2.m: With formulas ending in "svāhā", he places [the cakes] on the fire: “O divine Aśvins, with the honey-whip sprinkle today this sacrifice for the sacrificer! Sacrifice the oblation for Indra, for the gods! / O divine Viṣṇu, stride widely today at this sacrifice for the sacrificer! Sacrifice the oblation for Indra, for the gods! / O divine Soma, be the bestower of seed today at this sacrifice for the sacrificer! Sacrifice the oblation for Indra, for the gods! / O divine Dhātṛ, be a good supporter today at this sacrifice for the sacrificer! Sacrifice the oblation for Indra, for the gods! / O divine pressing stones, speak honeyed speech today at this sacrifice for the sacrificer! Sacrifice the oblation for Indra, for the gods! / O divine Anumati, approve today of this sacrifice for the sacrificer! Sacrifice the oblation for Indra, for the gods! / O divine Aditi, generate a good descendant today at this sacrifice for the sacrificer! Sacrifice the oblation for Indra, for the gods! / Sadas-dweller, rich in offspring, Ribhu, gracious, wise! Sacrifice the oblation for Indra, for the gods! / O divine Tvaṣṭṛ, be a bestower of good seed today at this sacrifice for the sacrificer! Sacrifice the oblation for Indra, for the gods!”
There are an agniṣṭoma, two ukthya days, and an atirātra.
The Saṃsarpa of Vasiṣṭha; one desiring offspring should sacrifice.
There are an agniṣṭoma, two ukthya days, and an atirātra.
The Saṃjaya of Viśvāmitra; a king desiring victory should sacrifice.

9.4.2.s: trivṛd agniṣṭomaḥ pañcadaśa ukthyaḥ saptadaśa ukthya ekavim̐śo 'tirātraḥ /
9.4.2.d: त्रिवृद् अग्निष्टोमः पञ्चदश उक्थ्यः सप्तदश उक्थ्य एकविम्̐शो ऽतिरात्रः /
9.4.2.m: There are a trivṛt agniṣṭoma, a fifteen-fold ukthya, a seventeen-fold ukthya, and a twenty-one-fold atirātra.

9.4.2.s: viśveṣāṃ devānām abhyāsaṅgyaḥ pañcāho bhrātṛvyavān svargakāmaḥ paśukāmo vā yajeta /
9.4.2.d: विश्वेषां देवानाम् अभ्यासङ्ग्यः पञ्चाहो भ्रातृव्यवान् स्वर्गकामः पशुकामो वा यजेत /
9.4.2.m: The Abhyāsaṅgya of the Viśvedevas is a five-day rite; one who has rivals, one who desires heaven, or one who desires cattle should sacrifice.

9.4.2.s: āditaḥ pañcāho daśarātrikaḥ / pañcame rātrir mahatām /
9.4.2.d: आदितः पञ्चाहो दशरात्रिकः / पञ्चमे रात्रिर् महताम् /
9.4.2.m: From the beginning, it is a five-day period of the ten-day form; on the fifth day, there is the night [rite] of the Mahats.
One wishing to obtain abundance should sacrifice with the Marutstoma of five autumns.
On the new-moon day of Vaiśākha, on the day of sacrifice, he fasts for the animal sacrifice.
He dedicates seventeen dappled, three-year-old heifers that have not been covered.

9.4.2.d: सप्तदश पृश्नीन् उक्ष्णो ऽनडुहः पञ्चवर्षान् अनूपर्ध्यति /
9.4.2.m: Alongside them he sets seventeen dappled five-year-old bulls, draft oxen.
In the case of all animals to be sacrificed, dedication, sprinkling, leading near, and carrying fire around [are performed].
There is releasing of the bulls, and they conclude [the rite] with the other [female animals].

9.4.2.s: prāyaścittāni / yadi prāsahā hareyur indrāyāprasahyāyaikādaśakapālaṃ nirupyāthānyaṃ tadrūpaṃ tadvarṇaṃ tadvayasam upākaroti /
9.4.2.d: प्रायश्चित्तानि / यदि प्रासहा हरेयुर् इन्द्रायाप्रसह्यायैकादशकपालं निरुप्याथान्यं तद्रूपं तद्वर्णं तद्वयसम् उपाकरोति /
9.4.2.m: The expiations: if [robbers] carry [an animal] off by force, having apportioned [a cake] on eleven potsherds to Indra the Unassailable, he then dedicates another of the same form, the same colour, and the same age.

9.4.2.s: yadi kūṭaḥ kāṇaḥ śroṇau vā bārhaspatyaṃ carum̐ yadi kāṇo vaiva sauryam ekakapālam̐ yadi svabhraṃ gartam̐ vā bhaumam ekakapālam̐ yadi patetvāyavyaṃ carum̐ yady avasīden nairṛtaṃ carum̐ yady anyo 'nyenāpatāyeta prājāpatyaṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ nirupyāthānyaṃ tadrūpaṃ tadvarṇaṃ tadvayasam upākaroti /
9.4.2.d: यदि कूटः काणः श्रोणौ वा बार्हस्पत्यं चरुम्̐ यदि काणो वैव सौर्यम् एककपालम्̐ यदि स्वभ्रं गर्तम्̐ वा भौमम् एककपालम्̐ यदि पतेत्वायव्यं चरुम्̐ यद्य् अवसीदेन् नैरृतं चरुम्̐ यद्य् अन्यो ऽन्येनापतायेत प्राजापत्यं द्वादशकपालं निरुप्याथान्यं तद्रूपं तद्वर्णं तद्वयसम् उपाकरोति /
9.4.2.m: If [an animal] is hornless, one-eyed, or lame, [he offers] a boiled oblation to Bṛhaspati; or if it is just one-eyed, [a cake] on one potsherd to Sūrya; if it falls into a pit or a hole, [a cake] on one potsherd to Bhūmi; if it falls down, a boiled oblation to Vāyu; if it collapses, a boiled oblation to Nirṛti; if they run into each other, having apportioned [a cake] on twelve potsherds to Prajāpati, he then dedicates another of the same form, the same colour, and the same age.

9.4.2.s: marutyo vatsataryaḥ sam̐vatsare rājīvatyo dvitīye kalmāṣāḥ tṛtīye navanītapṛśnīr aruṇāś caturthe piśaṅgīḥ pañcame /
9.4.2.d: मरुत्यो वत्सतर्यः सम्̐वत्सरे राजीवत्यो द्वितीये कल्माषाः तृतीये नवनीतपृश्नीर् अरुणाश् चतुर्थे पिशङ्गीः पञ्चमे /
9.4.2.m: The heifers are sacred to the Maruts: in the [first] year striped ones, in the second spotted ones, in the third butter-dappled ones, in the fourth reddish ones, in the fifth dun-coloured ones.
On this day of sacrifice, he undergoes consecration for the Soma rituals.
There are eighteen days of consecration and twelve upasads.

9.4.2.s: trivṛd agniṣṭomaḥ pañcadaśa ukthyaḥ pañcadaśo 'tirātraḥ saptadaśo 'tirātraḥ /
9.4.2.d: त्रिवृद् अग्निष्टोमः पञ्चदश उक्थ्यः पञ्चदशो ऽतिरात्रः सप्तदशो ऽतिरात्रः /
9.4.2.m: [The days are:] a trivṛt agniṣṭoma, a fifteenfold ukthya, a fifteenfold atirātra, and a seventeenfold atirātra.

9.4.2.s: aindrāmarutā ukṣāṇaḥ savanīyās traya ekasminn ahani pañcottame /
9.4.2.d: ऐन्द्रामरुता उक्षाणः सवनीयास् त्रय एकस्मिन्न् अहनि पञ्चोत्तमे /
9.4.2.m: Draft bulls sacred to Indra and the Maruts are the animals connected with the pressings: three on each day, [and] five on the last.

9.4.3.m: Desiring food-sustenance, one should perform Prajāpati's rite containing the vow.

9.4.3.s: jyotir agniṣṭomo gaur ukthyo mahāvrataṃ gaur ukthyo āyur atirātraḥ /
9.4.3.d: ज्योतिर् अग्निष्टोमो गौर् उक्थ्यो महाव्रतं गौर् उक्थ्यो आयुर् अतिरात्रः /
9.4.3.m: [It consists of:] a jyotis agniṣṭoma, a go ukthya, a mahāvrata, a go ukthya, [and] an āyus atirātra.
[Next is] the six-day rite of the Seasons; desiring firm standing, one should sacrifice [with it].
[It consists of:] a pṛṣṭhya six-day rite, a thirty-three-fold [stoma] thrice.
Desiring virile strength, one should sacrifice with Indra's combined [rite].

9.4.3.s: trivṛd agniṣṭomaḥ pañcadaśa ukthyaḥ saptadaśa ukthyo jyotir gaur āyur atirātraḥ /
9.4.3.d: त्रिवृद् अग्निष्टोमः पञ्चदश उक्थ्यः सप्तदश उक्थ्यो ज्योतिर् गौर् आयुर् अतिरात्रः /
9.4.3.m: [It consists of:] a trivṛt agniṣṭoma, a fifteenfold ukthya, a seventeenfold ukthya, a jyotis, a go, [and] an āyus atirātra.
A king desiring conquest should sacrifice with the Gods' Support of the Pṛṣṭhya.
[It consists of:] an abhyāsaṅgya five-day rite [and] a viśvajit atirātra.
Desiring prosperity, one should sacrifice with the seven-day rite of the Ṛṣis.
[It consists of:] a pṛṣṭhya six-day rite and a mahāvrata becoming an atirātra.
[Next is] the second [rite] of Prajāpati; desiring progeny, one should sacrifice [with it].
[It consists of:] a pṛṣṭhya six-day rite and a seventeenfold mahāvrata becoming an atirātra.
[Next is] the third [rite], of the Ādityas; desiring livestock, one should sacrifice [with it].
[It consists of:] a pṛṣṭhya six-day rite and a chandoma-pavamāna mahāvrata becoming an atirātra.

9.4.3.s: jamadagneś caturtho / parimitāṃ puṣṭim ichan yajeta /
9.4.3.d: जमदग्नेश् चतुर्थो / परिमितां पुष्टिम् इछन् यजेत /
9.4.3.m: [Next is] the fourth [rite], of Jamadagni; desiring abundant prosperity, one should sacrifice [with it].

9.4.3.s: abhyāsaṅgyaḥ pañcāhas trayastrim̐śam̐ ṣaṣṭham ahaḥ saptadaśaṃ mahāvratam atirātrabhūtam /
9.4.3.d: अभ्यासङ्ग्यः पञ्चाहस् त्रयस्त्रिम्̐शम्̐ षष्ठम् अहः सप्तदशं महाव्रतम् अतिरात्रभूतम् /
9.4.3.m: [It consists of:] an abhyāsaṅgya five-day rite, a thirty-three-fold sixth day, and a seventeenfold mahāvrata becoming an atirātra.
[Next is] the fifth [rite], of Indra; desiring virile strength, one should sacrifice [with it].

9.4.3.d: त्रिकद्रुकत्र्यहो ऽभिजिद् विश्वजित् सर्वजित् सर्वस्तोमो ऽतिरात्रः /
9.4.3.m: [It consists of:] a trikadruka three-day rite, an abhijit, a viśvajit, a sarvajit, [and] an all-stoma atirātra.
[Next is] Prajāpati's Janaka seven-day rite; desiring progeny, one should sacrifice [with it].

9.4.3.s: catvāri trivṛd ahāny agniṣṭomam ukhyāni viśvajin mahāvrataṃ jyotir atirātraḥ /
9.4.3.d: चत्वारि त्रिवृद् अहान्य् अग्निष्टोमम् उख्यानि विश्वजिन् महाव्रतं ज्योतिर् अतिरात्रः /
9.4.3.m: [It consists of:] four trivṛt days having the ukthya [form within an] agniṣṭoma, a viśvajit mahāvrata, [and] a jyotis atirātra.

9.4.3.s: devānāṃ pṛṣṭhyastoma ubhau kāmāv avarurutsamāno yajeta yo yajñaḥ sattre ca /
9.4.3.d: देवानां पृष्ठ्यस्तोम उभौ कामाव् अवरुरुत्समानो यजेत यो यज्ञः सत्त्रे च /
9.4.3.m: Desiring to obtain both desires—whatever [fruit belongs to] an individual sacrifice and in a sacrificial session—one should sacrifice with the Gods' Pṛṣṭhyastoma.
[It consists of:] a pṛṣṭhya six-day rite with the Bṛhat and Rathaṃtara chants, [and] a viśvajit atirātra.
Desiring godhead, one should sacrifice with the eight-day rite of the Vasus.
[It consists of:] a pṛṣṭhya six-day rite, a mahāvrata, [and] a jyotis atirātra.
Desiring a long life, one should sacrifice with the nine-day rite of the Gods.

9.4.3.s: pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍaho jyotir gaur āyur atirātraḥ /
9.4.3.d: पृष्ठ्यः षडहो ज्योतिर् गौर् आयुर् अतिरात्रः /
9.4.3.m: [It consists of:] a pṛṣṭhya six-day rite, a jyotis, a go, [and] an āyus atirātra.
Desiring livestock, one should sacrifice with the second [rite] of the Ādityas.
[It consists of:] a trikadruka three-day rite, an abhyāsaṅgya five-day rite, [and] a viśvajit atirātra.

9.4.3.s: indrasya trikakud daśarātraḥ / pāpmano mokṣamāṇo yajeta /
9.4.3.d: इन्द्रस्य त्रिककुद् दशरात्रः / पाप्मनो मोक्षमाणो यजेत /
9.4.3.m: Desiring release from evil, one should sacrifice with Indra's three-peaked ten-day rite.

9.4.3.s: trivṛtāv agniṣṭomau pañcadaśa ukthyo madhye saptadaśāv agniṣṭomāv ekavim̐śa ukthyo madhye ... /
9.4.3.d: त्रिवृताव् अग्निष्टोमौ पञ्चदश उक्थ्यो मध्ये सप्तदशाव् अग्निष्टोमाव् एकविम्̐श उक्थ्यो मध्ये ... /
9.4.3.m: [It consists of:] two trivṛt agniṣṭomas with a fifteenfold ukthya in between, two seventeenfold agniṣṭomas with a twenty-one-fold ukthya in between, […]

9.4.3.s: trayas trivṛto 'gniṣṭomās trayaḥ pañcadaśā ukthyās trayaḥ saptadaśā ukthyā ekavim̐śo 'tirātraḥ /
9.4.3.d: त्रयस् त्रिवृतो ऽग्निष्टोमास् त्रयः पञ्चदशा उक्थ्यास् त्रयः सप्तदशा उक्थ्या एकविम्̐शो ऽतिरात्रः /
9.4.3.m: [It consists of:] three trivṛt agniṣṭomas, three fifteenfold ukthyas, three seventeenfold ukthyas, [and] a twenty-one-fold atirātra.
[Next is] the chandoma ten-day rite of the Ādityas; desiring livestock, one should sacrifice [with it].

9.4.3.s: abhyāsaṅgyaḥ pañcāhaś catvāraś chandomā viśvajid atirātraḥ /
9.4.3.d: अभ्यासङ्ग्यः पञ्चाहश् चत्वारश् छन्दोमा विश्वजिद् अतिरात्रः /
9.4.3.m: [It consists of:] an abhyāsaṅgya five-day rite, four chandomas, [and] a viśvajit atirātra.
One who is being practiced against with sorcery should sacrifice with the Gods' Citadel ten-day rite.

9.4.3.s: trivṛd agniṣṭomo jyotir ukthyas trivṛd agniṣṭomo gaur ukthyo 'bhijid agniṣṭomo gaur ukthyo viśvajid agniṣṭoma āyur ukthyo viśvajid agniṣṭomaḥ sarvastomo 'tirātraḥ /
9.4.3.d: त्रिवृद् अग्निष्टोमो ज्योतिर् उक्थ्यस् त्रिवृद् अग्निष्टोमो गौर् उक्थ्यो ऽभिजिद् अग्निष्टोमो गौर् उक्थ्यो विश्वजिद् अग्निष्टोम आयुर् उक्थ्यो विश्वजिद् अग्निष्टोमः सर्वस्तोमो ऽतिरात्रः /
9.4.3.m: [It consists of:] a trivṛt agniṣṭoma, a jyotis ukthya, a trivṛt agniṣṭoma, a go ukthya, an abhijit agniṣṭoma, a go ukthya, a viśvajit agniṣṭoma, an āyus ukthya, a viśvajit agniṣṭoma, [and] an all-stoma atirātra.

9.4.3.s: kṣemadhanvā pauṇḍarīka ekādaśarātreṇa yajeta pārameṣṭhyakāmaḥ svārājyakāmo vā /
9.4.3.d: क्षेमधन्वा पौण्डरीक एकादशरात्रेण यजेत पारमेष्ठ्यकामः स्वाराज्यकामो वा /
9.4.3.m: Kṣemadhanvan, desiring pre-eminence or desiring self-rule, should sacrifice with the Pauṇḍarīka eleven-day rite.

9.4.3.d: ... अन्वहम्̐ विहृत्य सहस्राणि ददाति चतुष्टोमे ऽश्वसहस्रम् /
9.4.3.m: […] day by day, distributing [them], he gives thousands [of cows], [and] a thousand horses at the four-stoma [rite].
The twelve-day rite is explained; the twelve-day rite [is the archetype].

9.5.1.s: atreṣv abhiplavam̐ ṣaḍahaṃ pratīyād daśarātre dvādaśāhasya daśāhāny anyat prāyaṇīyodayanīyābhyāṃ pañcāhe jyotir gaur āyur iti trikadrukaṃ pañcāhaṃ navarātre 'bhijitam̐ svarasāmno viṣuvatam āvṛttān svarasāmno viśvajitam̐ sarvapṛṣṭhaṃ trirātre jyotir gaur āyur iti trirātraṃ trayastrim̐śārambhaṇe pratilomaṃ pṛṣṭham upottamam̐ vratam anādeśe /
9.5.1.d: अत्रेष्व् अभिप्लवम्̐ षडहं प्रतीयाद् दशरात्रे द्वादशाहस्य दशाहान्य् अन्यत् प्रायणीयोदयनीयाभ्यां पञ्चाहे ज्योतिर् गौर् आयुर् इति त्रिकद्रुकं पञ्चाहं नवरात्रे ऽभिजितम्̐ स्वरसाम्नो विषुवतम् आवृत्तान् स्वरसाम्नो विश्वजितम्̐ सर्वपृष्ठं त्रिरात्रे ज्योतिर् गौर् आयुर् इति त्रिरात्रं त्रयस्त्रिम्̐शारम्भणे प्रतिलोमं पृष्ठम् उपोत्तमम्̐ व्रतम् अनादेशे /
9.5.1.m: In these [rites], one should understand an abhiplava six-day rite [wherever a six-day rite is meant]; in a ten-day rite, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, other than the introductory and concluding [days]; in a five-day rite, the trikadruka five-day rite [comprising] jyotis, go, and āyus; in a nine-day rite, the abhijit, the svarasāmans, the viṣuvat, the reversed svarasāmans, [and] the viśvajit with all the pṛṣṭhas; in a three-day rite, the three-day rite of jyotis, go, and āyus; at the commencement of a thirty-three-fold stoma, the reverse pṛṣṭha; in the absence of an explicit rule, the rite [mahāvrata] is next to the last.

9.5.1.s: dvādaśāhaprabhṛtīni sattrāṇy ubhayato'tirātrāṇy aharabhyuccayenā catvārim̐śād rātrāt /
9.5.1.d: द्वादशाहप्रभृतीनि सत्त्राण्य् उभयतोऽतिरात्राण्य् अहरभ्युच्चयेना चत्वारिम्̐शाद् रात्रात् /
9.5.1.m: The sacrificial sessions, beginning with the twelve-day rite, have atirātras at both ends, with the addition of a day up to forty nights.

9.5.1.s: teṣām ahaḥkḷptiḥ /
9.5.1.d: तेषाम् अहःकॢप्तिः /

9.5.1.s: dvādaśāhe purastācchanomānām̐ sarvastomo 'tirātra ṛddhikāmās trayodaśarātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.1.d: द्वादशाहे पुरस्ताच्छनोमानाम्̐ सर्वस्तोमो ऽतिरात्र ऋद्धिकामास् त्रयोदशरात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.1.m: Desiring prosperity, they should undertake a thirteen-day rite: in the twelve-day rite, an all-stoma atirātra before the chandomas.

9.5.1.s: upottamam̐ vratam uttarasya / pratiṣṭhākāmās trayodaśarātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.1.d: उपोत्तमम्̐ व्रतम् उत्तरस्य / प्रतिष्ठाकामास् त्रयोदशरात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.1.m: In the following [rite], the vow [mahāvrata] is next to the last; desiring firm standing, they should undertake a thirteen-day rite.

9.5.1.s: dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni viṣuvān devatvakāmās trayodaśarātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.1.d: द्वादशाहस्य दशाहानि विषुवान् देवत्वकामास् त्रयोदशरात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.1.m: [In the third, there are] the ten days of the twelve-day rite [and] a viṣuvat; desiring godhead, they should undertake a thirteen-day rite.

9.5.1.s: caturvim̐śa ukthyo navarātro mahāvrataṃ pratiṣṭhākāmās trayodaśarātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.1.d: चतुर्विम्̐श उक्थ्यो नवरात्रो महाव्रतं प्रतिष्ठाकामास् त्रयोदशरात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.1.m: [In the fourth, there is] a twenty-four-fold ukthya, a nine-day rite, [and] the mahāvrata; desiring firm standing, they should undertake a thirteen-day rite.

9.5.1.s: goāyuṣī daśarātraḥ / pratiṣṭhākāmāś caturdaśarātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.1.d: गोआयुषी दशरात्रः / प्रतिष्ठाकामाश् चतुर्दशरात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.1.m: The Go and Āyus [days and] the ten-day rite: those desiring a firm foundation should undertake the fourteen-day rite.

9.5.1.s: pṛṣṭhya āvṛttaḥ pṛṣṭhyo devatvakāmāś caturdaśarātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.1.d: पृष्ठ्य आवृत्तः पृष्ठ्यो देवत्वकामाश् चतुर्दशरात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.1.m: A Pṛṣṭhya, [then] a reversed Pṛṣṭhya: those desiring divine status should undertake the fourteen-day rite.

9.5.1.s: ubhayatastrirātrābhyāṃ pṛṣṭhyo yām̐s talpa udake vā vivāhe mīmām̐seram̐s ta eva caturdaśarātram epeyuḥ /
9.5.1.d: उभयतस्त्रिरात्राभ्यां पृष्ठ्यो याम्̐स् तल्प उदके वा विवाहे मीमाम्̐सेरम्̐स् त एव चतुर्दशरात्रम् एपेयुः /
9.5.1.m: A Pṛṣṭhya flanked on both sides by three-day rites: those whom [people] would doubt regarding marriage bed or water, they indeed should undertake the fourteen-day rite.

9.5.1.s: pṛṣṭhyo mahāvrataṃ pṛṣṭhyas trayastrim̐śārambhaṇo yathā vaikāṣṭakāyāṃ mahāvratam̐ syād vratād brahmavarcasakāmāḥ pañcadaśarātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.1.d: पृष्ठ्यो महाव्रतं पृष्ठ्यस् त्रयस्त्रिम्̐शारम्भणो यथा वैकाष्टकायां महाव्रतम्̐ स्याद् व्रताद् ब्रह्मवर्चसकामाः पञ्चदशरात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.1.m: A Pṛṣṭhya, the Mahāvrata, a Pṛṣṭhya beginning with the thirty-three-versed [stoma], or just as the Mahāvrata may be on the Ekāṣṭakā: from [that] vow, those desiring spiritual radiance should undertake the fifteen-day rite.

9.5.1.s: trivṛdagniṣṭud agniṣṭoma ubhayatastrirātrābhyāṃ pṛṣṭhyo brahmavarcasakāmāḥ pañcadaśarātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.1.d: त्रिवृदग्निष्टुद् अग्निष्टोम उभयतस्त्रिरात्राभ्यां पृष्ठ्यो ब्रह्मवर्चसकामाः पञ्चदशरात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.1.m: A nine-versed Agniṣṭut Agniṣṭoma, a Pṛṣṭhya flanked on both sides by three-day rites: those desiring spiritual radiance should undertake the fifteen-day rite.

9.5.1.s: trivṛdagniṣṭud agniṣṭomas trirātro daśarātraś cānya uttarato 'tirātraḥ / sattre yajñe carddhikāmam ichanta etaṃ pañcadaśarātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.1.d: त्रिवृदग्निष्टुद् अग्निष्टोमस् त्रिरात्रो दशरात्रश् चान्य उत्तरतो ऽतिरात्रः / सत्त्रे यज्ञे चर्द्धिकामम् इछन्त एतं पञ्चदशरात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.1.m: A nine-versed Agniṣṭut Agniṣṭoma, a three-day rite, a ten-day rite, and another Atirātra at the end: those wishing for prosperous desire in sacrificial session or sacrifice should undertake this fifteen-day rite.

9.5.1.s: etāsv eva vratam̐ vijitikāmāḥ ṣoḍaśarātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.1.d: एतास्व् एव व्रतम्̐ विजितिकामाः षोडशरात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.1.m: With the vow [day added] to these very [days]: those desiring complete victory should undertake the sixteen-day rite.

9.5.1.s: pañcāho daśarātraḥ / śrīkāmāḥ saptadaśarātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.1.d: पञ्चाहो दशरात्रः / श्रीकामाः सप्तदशरात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.1.m: A five-day rite, a ten-day rite: those desiring prosperity should undertake the seventeen-day rite.

9.5.1.s: ṣaḍaho daśarātra āyuḥkāmā aṣṭādaśarātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.1.d: षडहो दशरात्र आयुःकामा अष्टादशरात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.1.m: A six-day rite, a ten-day rite: those desiring long life should undertake the eighteen-day rite.

9.5.1.s: etāsv eva vrataṃ / ... /
9.5.1.d: एतास्व् एव व्रतं / ... /

9.5.1.s: ... / brahmavarcasakāmā vim̐śatirātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.1.d: ... / ब्रह्मवर्चसकामा विम्̐शतिरात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.1.m: [...]: those desiring spiritual radiance should undertake the twenty-day rite.

9.5.1.s: pṛṣṭhyaḥ svarasāmāno viṣuvān āvṛttāḥ svarasāmānaḥ pṛṣṭhyas trayastrim̐śārambhaṇo 'nnādyakāmā ekavim̐śatirātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.1.d: पृष्ठ्यः स्वरसामानो विषुवान् आवृत्ताः स्वरसामानः पृष्ठ्यस् त्रयस्त्रिम्̐शारम्भणो ऽन्नाद्यकामा एकविम्̐शतिरात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.1.m: A Pṛṣṭhya, the Svarasāman days, the Viṣuvant, reversed Svarasāman days, a Pṛṣṭhya beginning with the thirty-three-versed [stoma]: those desiring food and proper nourishment should undertake the twenty-one-day rite.

9.5.1.s: trayaḥ ṣaḍahā ūrdhvaṃ prathamād atirātro 'nnādyakāmā ekavim̐śatirātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.1.d: त्रयः षडहा ऊर्ध्वं प्रथमाद् अतिरात्रो ऽन्नाद्यकामा एकविम्̐शतिरात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.1.m: Three six-day rites above the first, [then] an Atirātra: those desiring food and proper nourishment should undertake the twenty-one-day rite.

9.5.1.s: tryahaḥ ṣaḍaho daśarātro mahāvrataṃ paśukāmā dvāvim̐śatirātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.1.d: त्र्यहः षडहो दशरात्रो महाव्रतं पशुकामा द्वाविम्̐शतिरात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.1.m: A three-day rite, a six-day rite, a ten-day rite, the Mahāvrata: those desiring cattle should undertake the twenty-two-day rite.

9.5.1.s: pañcāhaḥ ṣaḍaho daśarātraḥ / pratiṣṭhākāmās trayovim̐śatirātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.1.d: पञ्चाहः षडहो दशरात्रः / प्रतिष्ठाकामास् त्रयोविम्̐शतिरात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.1.m: A five-day rite, a six-day rite, a ten-day rite: those desiring a firm foundation should undertake the twenty-three-day rite.

9.5.1.s: sam̐sadāmayanaṃ / pṛṣṭhyastomaḥ ṣaḍahas trayastrim̐śamahar aniruktam upahavyakḷptaṃ trayastrim̐śam ahar niruktaṃ triṇavaṃ dve ekavim̐śe triṇavaṃ trayastrim̐śam ahar niruktaṃ trayastrim̐śam ahar aniruktaṃ pṛṣṭhyastomaḥ ṣaḍahaḥ pratyaṅ trivṛd ahar aniruktaṃ jyotiṣṭomo 'gniṣṭomo 'nnādyakāmāś caturvim̐śatirātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.1.d: सम्̐सदामयनं / पृष्ठ्यस्तोमः षडहस् त्रयस्त्रिम्̐शमहर् अनिरुक्तम् उपहव्यकॢप्तं त्रयस्त्रिम्̐शम् अहर् निरुक्तं त्रिणवं द्वे एकविम्̐शे त्रिणवं त्रयस्त्रिम्̐शम् अहर् निरुक्तं त्रयस्त्रिम्̐शम् अहर् अनिरुक्तं पृष्ठ्यस्तोमः षडहः प्रत्यङ् त्रिवृद् अहर् अनिरुक्तं ज्योतिष्टोमो ऽग्निष्टोमो ऽन्नाद्यकामाश् चतुर्विम्̐शतिरात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.1.m: The Saṃsadāmayana rite: a Pṛṣṭhyastoma six-day rite, a non-enunciated thirty-three-versed day arranged like an Upahavya, an enunciated thirty-three-versed day, a twenty-seven-versed day, two twenty-one-versed days, a twenty-seven-versed day, an enunciated thirty-three-versed day, a non-enunciated thirty-three-versed day, a Pṛṣṭhyastoma six-day rite backwards, a non-enunciated nine-versed day, a Jyotiṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma: those desiring food and proper nourishment should undertake the twenty-four-day rite.

9.5.1.s: ṣaḍahau daśarātro 'nnādyakāmāś caturvim̐śatirātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.1.d: षडहौ दशरात्रो ऽन्नाद्यकामाश् चतुर्विम्̐शतिरात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.1.m: Two six-day rites, a ten-day rite: those desiring food and proper nourishment should undertake the twenty-four-day rite.

9.5.1.s: etāsv eva vrataṃ brahmavarcasakāmāḥ pañcavim̐śatirātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.1.d: एतास्व् एव व्रतं ब्रह्मवर्चसकामाः पञ्चविम्̐शतिरात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.1.m: With the vow [day added] to these very [days]: those desiring spiritual radiance should undertake the twenty-five-day rite.

9.5.1.s: etāsv eva goāyuṣīpurastātṣaḍahānāṃ na vratam̐ vijitikāmāḥ ṣaḍvim̐śatirātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.1.d: एतास्व् एव गोआयुषीपुरस्तात्षडहानां न व्रतम्̐ विजितिकामाः षड्विम्̐शतिरात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.1.m: With the Go and Āyus [days] before the six-day rites to these very [days, and] no vow [day]: those desiring complete victory should undertake the twenty-six-day rite.

9.5.1.s: etāsv eva tryahaḥ purastātṣaḍahānāṃ na goāyuṣī / śrīkāmāḥ saptavim̐śatirātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.1.d: एतास्व् एव त्र्यहः पुरस्तात्षडहानां न गोआयुषी / श्रीकामाः सप्तविम्̐शतिरात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.1.m: With a three-day rite before the six-day rites to these very [days, and] no Go and Āyus [days]: those desiring prosperity should undertake the twenty-seven-day rite.

9.5.1.s: etāsv eva vratam āyuḥkāmā aṣṭāvim̐śatirātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.1.d: एतास्व् एव व्रतम् आयुःकामा अष्टाविम्̐शतिरात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.1.m: With the vow [day added] to these very [days]: those desiring long life should undertake the twenty-eight-day rite.

9.5.1.s: pañcāhaḥ ṣaḍahau daśarātro brahmavarcasakāmā ekonatrim̐śadrātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.1.d: पञ्चाहः षडहौ दशरात्रो ब्रह्मवर्चसकामा एकोनत्रिम्̐शद्रात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.1.m: A five-day rite, two six-day rites, a ten-day rite: those desiring spiritual radiance should undertake the twenty-nine-day rite.

9.5.1.s: trayaḥ ṣaḍahā daśarātraḥ / puruṣakāmās trim̐śadrātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.1.d: त्रयः षडहा दशरात्रः / पुरुषकामास् त्रिम्̐शद्रात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.1.m: Three six-day rites, a ten-day rite: those desiring offspring should undertake the thirty-day rite.

9.5.1.s: etāsv eva vratam ojaskāmā ekatrim̐śadrātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.1.d: एतास्व् एव व्रतम् ओजस्कामा एकत्रिम्̐शद्रात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.1.m: With the vow [day added] to these very [days]: those desiring vigor should undertake the thirty-one-day rite.

9.5.1.s: etāsv eva goāyuṣīpurastātṣaḍahānāṃ na vrataṃ paśukāmā dvātrim̐śadrātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.1.d: एतास्व् एव गोआयुषीपुरस्तात्षडहानां न व्रतं पशुकामा द्वात्रिम्̐शद्रात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.1.m: With the Go and Āyus [days] before the six-day rites to these very [days, and] no vow [day]: those desiring cattle should undertake the thirty-two-day rite.

9.5.2.s: ā trayastrim̐śāt trayaḥ pṛṣṭhyāḥ pañcāhā viśvajid atirātraḥ pañcāho daśarātraḥ / pratiṣṭhākāmās trayastrim̐śadrātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.2.d: आ त्रयस्त्रिम्̐शात् त्रयः पृष्ठ्याः पञ्चाहा विश्वजिद् अतिरात्रः पञ्चाहो दशरात्रः / प्रतिष्ठाकामास् त्रयस्त्रिम्̐शद्रात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.2.m: Up to the thirty-three-versed [stoma], three Pṛṣṭhya five-day rites, a Viśvajit Atirātra, a five-day rite, a ten-day rite: those desiring a firm foundation should undertake the thirty-three-day rite.

9.5.2.s: trayaḥ ṣaḍahā madhyam abhito 'tirātrau daśarātro mahāvrataṃ pratiṣṭhākāmās trayastrim̐śadrātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.2.d: त्रयः षडहा मध्यम् अभितो ऽतिरात्रौ दशरात्रो महाव्रतं प्रतिष्ठाकामास् त्रयस्त्रिम्̐शद्रात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.2.m: Three six-day rites, two Atirātras flanking the middle, a ten-day rite, the Mahāvrata: those desiring a firm foundation should undertake the thirty-three-day rite.

9.5.2.s: trayaḥ pṛṣṭhyāḥ pañcāhā viśvajid atirātras trayaḥ pṛṣṭhyāḥ pañcāhāḥ / pratiṣṭhākāmās trayastrim̐śadrātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.2.d: त्रयः पृष्ठ्याः पञ्चाहा विश्वजिद् अतिरात्रस् त्रयः पृष्ठ्याः पञ्चाहाः / प्रतिष्ठाकामास् त्रयस्त्रिम्̐शद्रात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.2.m: Three Pṛṣṭhya five-day rites, a Viśvajit Atirātra, three Pṛṣṭhya five-day rites: those desiring a firm foundation should undertake the thirty-three-day rite.

9.5.2.s: tryahas trayaḥ ṣaḍahā daśarātro mahāvratam annādyakāmāś catustrim̐śadrātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.2.d: त्र्यहस् त्रयः षडहा दशरात्रो महाव्रतम् अन्नाद्यकामाश् चतुस्त्रिम्̐शद्रात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.2.m: A three-day rite, three six-day rites, a ten-day rite, the Mahāvrata: those desiring food and proper nourishment should undertake the thirty-four-day rite.

9.5.2.s: trayas trayaḥ ṣaḍahā daśarātro goāyuṣī / brahmavarcasakāmāḥ pañcatrim̐śadrātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.2.d: त्रयस् त्रयः षडहा दशरात्रो गोआयुषी / ब्रह्मवर्चसकामाः पञ्चत्रिम्̐शद्रात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.2.m: Three times three six-day rites, a ten-day rite, the Go and Āyus [days]: those desiring spiritual radiance should undertake the thirty-five-day rite.

9.5.2.s: catvāraḥ ṣaḍahā daśarātro vijitikāmāḥ ṣaṭtrim̐śadrātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.2.d: चत्वारः षडहा दशरात्रो विजितिकामाः षट्त्रिम्̐शद्रात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.2.m: Four six-day rites, a ten-day rite: those desiring complete victory should undertake the thirty-six-day rite.

9.5.2.s: etāsv eva vratam̐ śrīkāmāḥ saptatrim̐śadrātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.2.d: एतास्व् एव व्रतम्̐ श्रीकामाः सप्तत्रिम्̐शद्रात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.2.m: With the vow [day added] to these very [days]: those desiring prosperity should undertake the thirty-seven-day rite.

9.5.2.s: etāsv eva goāyuṣī purastāt ṣaḍahānāṃ na vratam āyuḥkāmā aṣṭātrim̐śadrātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.2.d: एतास्व् एव गोआयुषी पुरस्तात् षडहानां न व्रतम् आयुःकामा अष्टात्रिम्̐शद्रात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.2.m: With the Go and Āyus [days] before the six-day rites to these very [days, and] no vow [day]: those desiring long life should undertake the thirty-eight-day rite.

9.5.2.s: etāsv eva tryahaḥ purastāt ṣaḍahānāṃ na goāyuṣī / brahmavarcasakāmā ekonacatvārim̐śadrātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.2.d: एतास्व् एव त्र्यहः पुरस्तात् षडहानां न गोआयुषी / ब्रह्मवर्चसकामा एकोनचत्वारिम्̐शद्रात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.2.m: With a three-day rite before the six-day rites to these very [days, and] no Go and Āyus [days]: those desiring spiritual radiance should undertake the thirty-nine-day rite.

9.5.2.s: etāsv eva vrataṃ / puruṣakāmāś catvārim̐śadrātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.2.d: एतास्व् एव व्रतं / पुरुषकामाश् चत्वारिम्̐शद्रात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.2.m: With the vow [day added] to these very [days]: those desiring offspring should undertake the forty-day rite.

9.5.2.s: agniṣṭomo dvāv ukthyau trivṛt stomas trayāṇām atirātro navokthyāḥ ṣoḍaśī daśamaḥ pañcadaśastomā atirātro dvādaśokthyāḥ saptadaśastomā atirātraḥ pṛṣṭhyo 'tirātro dvādaśokthyā ekavim̐śastomā / vāyor vidhṛtir vi pāpmanā vartemahītikāmas ta etam ekonapañcāśadrātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.2.d: अग्निष्टोमो द्वाव् उक्थ्यौ त्रिवृत् स्तोमस् त्रयाणाम् अतिरात्रो नवोक्थ्याः षोडशी दशमः पञ्चदशस्तोमा अतिरात्रो द्वादशोक्थ्याः सप्तदशस्तोमा अतिरात्रः पृष्ठ्यो ऽतिरात्रो द्वादशोक्थ्या एकविम्̐शस्तोमा / वायोर् विधृतिर् वि पाप्मना वर्तेमहीतिकामस् त एतम् एकोनपञ्चाशद्रात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.2.m: An Agniṣṭoma, two Ukthyas, a nine-versed stoma for the three; an Atirātra, nine Ukthyas, the tenth a Ṣoḍaśin, [all] fifteen-versed stomas; an Atirātra, twelve Ukthyas, seventeen-versed stomas; an Atirātra, a Pṛṣṭhya; an Atirātra, twelve Ukthyas, twenty-one-versed stomas—desiring: 'May we, as Vāyu's support, turn away from evil', they should undertake this forty-nine-day rite.

9.5.2.s: pañcānām̐ ṣaḍahānāṃ dvayordvayoḥ purastād dvaudvāv atirātrau pañcamasya purastād dvādaśarātro mahāvrataṃ pratiṣṭhākāmās ta etam ekonapañcāśadrātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.2.d: पञ्चानाम्̐ षडहानां द्वयोर्द्वयोः पुरस्ताद् द्वौद्वाव् अतिरात्रौ पञ्चमस्य पुरस्ताद् द्वादशरात्रो महाव्रतं प्रतिष्ठाकामास् त एतम् एकोनपञ्चाशद्रात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.2.m: Of the five six-day rites, two Atirātras before each pair of two, a twelve-day rite before the fifth, the Mahāvrata: those desiring a firm foundation should undertake this forty-nine-day rite.

9.5.2.s: ṣaṇṇām̐ ṣaḍahānāṃ pañcamasya purastāt sarvastomo 'tirātraḥ ṣaṣṭhasyopariṣṭād daśarātraḥ /
9.5.2.d: षण्णाम्̐ षडहानां पञ्चमस्य पुरस्तात् सर्वस्तोमो ऽतिरात्रः षष्ठस्योपरिष्टाद् दशरात्रः /
9.5.2.m: Of six six-day rites, an all-versed Atirātra before the fifth, a ten-day rite after the sixth.

9.5.2.s: āñjīram̐ś cābhyañjīram̐ś ca teṣv ahaḥsu guggulaphāṇṭena prātaḥsavane saugandhikaphāṇṭena mādhyaṃdine savane pūtudāruphāṇṭena tṛtīyasavane prātaranuvākam anuvakṣyantaḥ prātaḥsavane prasarpantaś caivam uttarayoḥ savanayoḥ /
9.5.2.d: आञ्जीरम्̐श् चाभ्यञ्जीरम्̐श् च तेष्व् अहःसु गुग्गुलफाण्टेन प्रातःसवने सौगन्धिकफाण्टेन माध्यंदिने सवने पूतुदारुफाण्टेन तृतीयसवने प्रातरनुवाकम् अनुवक्ष्यन्तः प्रातःसवने प्रसर्पन्तश् चैवम् उत्तरयोः सवनयोः /
9.5.2.m: And on those days they should smear [the eyes] and anoint [the body]: with an infusion of guggulu at the morning pressing, with an infusion of saugandhika at the midday pressing, with an infusion of pūtudāru at the third pressing, when about to recite the morning recitation, and when gliding at the morning pressing; and in the same way at the subsequent two pressings.

9.5.2.s: ya ātmānaṃ naiva jānīram̐s ta etam ekonapañcāśadrātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.2.d: य आत्मानं नैव जानीरम्̐स् त एतम् एकोनपञ्चाशद्रात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.2.m: Those who do not even recognize themselves: they should undertake this forty-nine-day rite.

9.5.2.s: caturvim̐śa ukthyas trayaḥ ṣaḍahā navarātraḥ ṣaḍaho goāyuṣī daśarātro mahāvratam̐ sam̐vatsarasaṃmitam̐ sam̐vatsarakāmam ichantas ta etam ekonapañcāśadrātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.2.d: चतुर्विम्̐श उक्थ्यस् त्रयः षडहा नवरात्रः षडहो गोआयुषी दशरात्रो महाव्रतम्̐ सम्̐वत्सरसंमितम्̐ सम्̐वत्सरकामम् इछन्तस् त एतम् एकोनपञ्चाशद्रात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.2.m: A twenty-four-versed Ukthya, three six-day rites, a nine-day rite, a six-day rite, the Go and Āyus [days], a ten-day rite, the Mahāvrata, matching a year: wishing for the desire of a year, they should undertake this forty-nine-day rite.

9.5.2.s: agniṣṭomaḥ pañcokthyā agniṣṭomāv abhita ukthyo madhye trivṛtstomo navānām etena kalpena trayo navarātrā vyākhyātāḥ pañcadaśasaptadaśaikavim̐śastomā daśarātro mahāvratam̐ sāvitraṃ kakubhaṃ prasavakāmās ta etam ekonapañcāśadrātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.2.d: अग्निष्टोमः पञ्चोक्थ्या अग्निष्टोमाव् अभित उक्थ्यो मध्ये त्रिवृत्स्तोमो नवानाम् एतेन कल्पेन त्रयो नवरात्रा व्याख्याताः पञ्चदशसप्तदशैकविम्̐शस्तोमा दशरात्रो महाव्रतम्̐ सावित्रं ककुभं प्रसवकामास् त एतम् एकोनपञ्चाशद्रात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.2.m: An Agniṣṭoma, five Ukthyas, two Agniṣṭomas on both sides and an Ukthya in the middle, a nine-versed stoma for nine; by this procedure the three nine-day rites are explained, having fifteen-versed, seventeen-versed, and twenty-one-versed stomas, a ten-day rite, the Mahāvrata, Sāvitra, Kakubha: those desiring progeny should undertake this forty-nine-day rite.

9.5.2.s: tṛtīyenopottamo vyākhyātaḥ sarvastomasya sthāne mahāvrataṃ nāñjīrann ābhyañjīran vi pāpmanā vartemahītikāmās ta etam ekonapañcāśadrātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.2.d: तृतीयेनोपोत्तमो व्याख्यातः सर्वस्तोमस्य स्थाने महाव्रतं नाञ्जीरन्न् आभ्यञ्जीरन् वि पाप्मना वर्तेमहीतिकामास् त एतम् एकोनपञ्चाशद्रात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.2.m: The penultimate is explained by the third [form]: in place of the all-versed [Atirātra] is the Mahāvrata; they should not smear [their eyes] nor anoint [their bodies]; desiring: 'May we turn away from evil', they should undertake this forty-nine-day rite.

9.5.2.s: ṣaṭ ṣaḍahā daśarātro mahāvrataṃ pratiṣṭhākāmās ta etam ekonapañcāśadrātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.2.d: षट् षडहा दशरात्रो महाव्रतं प्रतिष्ठाकामास् त एतम् एकोनपञ्चाशद्रात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.2.m: Six six-day rites, a ten-day rite, the Mahāvrata: those desiring a firm foundation should undertake this forty-nine-day rite.

9.5.2.s: sam̐vatsarasaṃmite pṛṣṭhyāvadhikau purastādabhijita upariṣṭādviśvajita ṛddhikāmā ekaṣaṣṭirātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.2.d: सम्̐वत्सरसंमिते पृष्ठ्यावधिकौ पुरस्तादभिजित उपरिष्टाद्विश्वजित ऋद्धिकामा एकषष्टिरात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.2.m: In [a session] measured to a year, with two additional Pṛṣṭhya [six-day periods], [one] before the Abhijit and [one] after the Viśvajit, those desiring prosperity should undertake a sixty-one-day rite.

9.5.2.s: tryahaś caturdaśa ṣaḍahā daśarātro mahāvratam āyuḥkāmāḥ śatarātram upeyuḥ /
9.5.2.d: त्र्यहश् चतुर्दश षडहा दशरात्रो महाव्रतम् आयुःकामाः शतरात्रम् उपेयुः /
9.5.2.m: A three-day period, fourteen six-day periods, a ten-day period, [and] the Mahāvrata: those desiring a full life should undertake a hundred-day rite.

9.5.2.s: abhiprayāyam abhiṣuṇvanti samānatrābhiṣuṇvanti /
9.5.2.d: अभिप्रयायम् अभिषुण्वन्ति समानत्राभिषुण्वन्ति /
9.5.2.m: Moving forward, they press [the soma], or they press it in the same place.

9.5.2.s: dīkṣodavasānam̐ vā /
9.5.2.d: दीक्षोदवसानम्̐ वा /

9.5.2.s: āgneya aindāgno vaiṣṇavaḥ pauṣṇo vāyavya āśvinaḥ ṣaḍ atiriktāḥ paśavaḥ sattreṣu /
9.5.2.d: आग्नेय ऐन्दाग्नो वैष्णवः पौष्णो वायव्य आश्विनः षड् अतिरिक्ताः पशवः सत्त्रेषु /
9.5.2.m: Dedicated to Agni, to Indra-Agni, to Viṣṇu, to Pūṣan, to Vāyu, [and] to the Aśvins: [these are] the six surplus animal victims in the sacrificial sessions.

9.5.3.s: gavām ayanaṃ prajātikāmā upeyus tenādityānām ayanam̐ vyākhyātam aṅgirasāṃ ca /
9.5.3.d: गवाम् अयनं प्रजातिकामा उपेयुस् तेनादित्यानाम् अयनम्̐ व्याख्यातम् अङ्गिरसां च /
9.5.3.m: Those desiring offspring should undertake the Gavām Ayana. By it the Ādityānām Ayana is explained, and that of the Aṅgirases.

9.5.3.s: trivṛtpañcadaśastomaḥ ṣaḍahānāṃ purastāt pṛṣṭhyo māsānāṃ prāg viṣuvataḥ pañcadaśatrivṛd upariṣṭān madhye pṛṣṭhyo māsānām /
9.5.3.d: त्रिवृत्पञ्चदशस्तोमः षडहानां पुरस्तात् पृष्ठ्यो मासानां प्राग् विषुवतः पञ्चदशत्रिवृद् उपरिष्टान् मध्ये पृष्ठ्यो मासानाम् /
9.5.3.m: The Trivṛt-Pañcadaśa stoma is prior to the six-day periods, the Pṛṣṭhya [prior] to the months before the Viṣuvant; the Pañcadaśa-Trivṛt is after [it], in the middle [is] the Pṛṣṭhya of the months.

9.5.3.s: bṛhaspatisave 'bhijitaḥ sthāne viśvajita indrastomas tasmād uttaraḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍahaś ca daśarātro vyūḍhā agniṣṭomās trivṛta udbhidbalabhidau ca / so 'ṣṭāvim̐śatyahaḥ /
9.5.3.d: बृहस्पतिसवे ऽभिजितः स्थाने विश्वजित इन्द्रस्तोमस् तस्माद् उत्तरः पृष्ठ्यः षडहश् च दशरात्रो व्यूढा अग्निष्टोमास् त्रिवृत उद्भिद्बलभिदौ च / सो ऽष्टाविम्̐शत्यहः /
9.5.3.m: In place of the Abhijit is the Bṛhaspatisava, [and] in place of the Viśvajit is the Indrastoma; following that is a Pṛṣṭhya six-day period and a ten-day period, the Agniṣṭomas are rearranged as Trivṛt, and [there are] the Udbhid and Balabhid: that is a twenty-eight-day rite.

9.5.3.s: pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍaho madhye goāyuṣī avarūḍhastomaś chandomadaśāhaḥ /
9.5.3.d: पृष्ठ्यः षडहो मध्ये गोआयुषी अवरूढस्तोमश् छन्दोमदशाहः /
9.5.3.m: A Pṛṣṭhya six-day period is in the middle, the Go and Āyus [days], the Avarūḍhastoma, [and] the Chandoma-ten-day period.

9.5.3.s: gavām ayanena śeṣo vyākhyātaḥ svargakāmā upeyuḥ /
9.5.3.d: गवाम् अयनेन शेषो व्याख्यातः स्वर्गकामा उपेयुः /
9.5.3.m: The remainder is explained by the Gavām Ayana; those desiring heaven should undertake [it].

9.5.3.s: aṅgirasām ayanaṃ trivṛtstomaḥ ṣaḍahānāṃ purastāt pṛṣṭhyo māsānāṃ prāg viṣuvata ūrdhvam upariṣṭāt pṛṣṭhyo māsānām /
9.5.3.d: अङ्गिरसाम् अयनं त्रिवृत्स्तोमः षडहानां पुरस्तात् पृष्ठ्यो मासानां प्राग् विषुवत ऊर्ध्वम् उपरिष्टात् पृष्ठ्यो मासानाम् /
9.5.3.m: The Aṅgirasām Ayana: the Trivṛt stoma is before the six-day periods, the Pṛṣṭhya of the months is prior to the Viṣuvant; above, afterwards, is the Pṛṣṭhya of the months.

9.5.3.s: ṣaḍahayoś cāyuś ca gauś cānulomaś chandomadaśāhaḥ /
9.5.3.d: षडहयोश् चायुश् च गौश् चानुलोमश् छन्दोमदशाहः /
9.5.3.m: And of the two six-day periods, the Āyus and the Go, and in regular order the Chandoma-ten-day period.

9.5.3.s: ādityānām ayanena śeṣo vyākhyātaḥ / svargakāmā upeyuḥ /
9.5.3.d: आदित्यानाम् अयनेन शेषो व्याख्यातः / स्वर्गकामा उपेयुः /
9.5.3.m: The remainder is explained by the Ādityānām Ayana; those desiring heaven should undertake [it].

9.5.3.s: dṛtivātavator ayanaṃ pṛṣṭhyasyaikaikenāhnā prāg viṣuvato māsān yanti / viṣuvataḥ sthāne mahāvrataṃ tair evāvṛttair upariṣṭāt prathamottame ahanī sātirātre / ṛddhikāmā upeyuḥ /
9.5.3.d: दृतिवातवतोर् अयनं पृष्ठ्यस्यैकैकेनाह्ना प्राग् विषुवतो मासान् यन्ति / विषुवतः स्थाने महाव्रतं तैर् एवावृत्तैर् उपरिष्टात् प्रथमोत्तमे अहनी सातिरात्रे / ऋद्धिकामा उपेयुः /
9.5.3.m: The Dṛtivātavator Ayana: they proceed through the months with one single day of the Pṛṣṭhya [at a time] prior to the Viṣuvant; in place of the Viṣuvant is the Mahāvrata, [and] with those same [days] reversed, afterwards; the first and last days include Atirātras; those desiring prosperity should undertake [it].

9.5.3.s: kuṇḍapāyinām ayanaṃ māsaṃ dīkṣitā bhavanti / te māsi rājānaṃ krīṇanti /
9.5.3.d: कुण्डपायिनाम् अयनं मासं दीक्षिता भवन्ति / ते मासि राजानं क्रीणन्ति /
9.5.3.m: The Kuṇḍapāyinām Ayana: they are consecrated for a month; in [that] month they purchase the king [Soma].

9.5.3.s: dvādaśopasada uttamāyām upasady āparāhṇikīm̐ sam̐sthāpya somaṃ mahāvīrām̐ś ca nidhāyāgnihotreṇa darśapaurṇamāsābhyāṃ caturbhiś cāturmāsyaparvabhir ekaikena māsān yanti /
9.5.3.d: द्वादशोपसद उत्तमायाम् उपसद्य् आपराह्णिकीम्̐ सम्̐स्थाप्य सोमं महावीराम्̐श् च निधायाग्निहोत्रेण दर्शपौर्णमासाभ्यां चतुर्भिश् चातुर्मास्यपर्वभिर् एकैकेन मासान् यन्ति /
9.5.3.m: Twelve Upasads: having concluded the afternoon [Upasad] on the last Upasad day, having deposited the soma and the mahāvīra pots, they proceed through the months with the Agnihotra, with the New- and Full-Moon sacrifices, and with the four seasonal periods, one by one.

9.5.3.s: ardhamāsaṃ paurṇamāsīm ardhamāsam amāvāsyām̐ sam̐sthāpya śunāsīryam utsādya mahāvīrān agnipraṇayanaprabhṛti payodohanāntaṃ kṛtvā vasanti /
9.5.3.d: अर्धमासं पौर्णमासीम् अर्धमासम् अमावास्याम्̐ सम्̐स्थाप्य शुनासीर्यम् उत्साद्य महावीरान् अग्निप्रणयनप्रभृति पयोदोहनान्तं कृत्वा वसन्ति /
9.5.3.m: Having concluded the full-moon rite for half a month, [and] the new-moon rite for half a month, having celebrated the Śunāsīrya, having set aside the mahāvīra pots, having performed [the rites] beginning with the carrying forward of the fire and ending with the milking, they dwell [there].

9.5.3.s: śvobhūte prātaranuvākaprabhṛti pañcabhiḥ pṛṣṭhyāhobhir ekaikena māsān yanti /
9.5.3.d: श्वोभूते प्रातरनुवाकप्रभृति पञ्चभिः पृष्ठ्याहोभिर् एकैकेन मासान् यन्ति /
